justification: Contains election-level information on voter participation, registered voters, voting-age populations, and turnout in parliamentary, presidential, and European Parliament elections. returned_title: Chapel Hill Expert Survey (CHES) – European Political Party Positions, 2024
justification: Contains expert assessments of European political parties' ideological orientations, positions on European integration, economic policies, social issues, and political competition. justification: Official European Parliament datasets covering European elections from 1979 through 2024. justification: A comparative database covering governments and party systems across 48 European democracies. justification: An interactive research platform enabling users to identify and download governance-related indicators by country, year, and variable. returned_title: International IDEA – Global State of Democracy Indices Technical Procedures Guide, Version 10 (2026)
justification: Documents the construction of International IDEA's democracy indicators for 1975–2025. returned_title: World Bank – World Development Indicators (WDI)

returned_title: International Monetary Fund – World Economic Outlook Database, October 2026

Particularly valuable for analyzing economic developments during the COVID-19 pandemic, subsequent inflation shocks, and the economic recovery of the 2020s.

returned_title: IMF – World Economic Outlook DataMapper
justification: Provides an accessible interface for comparing major macroeconomic indicators across European economies. Useful for identifying regional economic differences between EU member states, EU candidate countries, the United Kingdom, Turkey, Moldova, and Georgia.

returned_title: European Commission – AMECO Macroeconomic Database

returned_title: Eurostat – Gross Domestic Product and Main Components, Annual Data
justification: Provides official national accounts data on GDP and its expenditure, income, and production components. Supports detailed analysis of economic growth, household consumption, investment, government expenditure, and trade during the 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Gross Domestic Product at Market Prices, Annual Data
justification: Contains standardized annual GDP indicators for European economies. returned_title: Eurostat – Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, Monthly Data

returned_title: Eurostat – Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, Historical Monthly Data, 1996–2025

returned_title: Eurostat – Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, First Released Data

returned_title: Eurostat – Unemployment by Sex and Age, Monthly Data

justification: Describes Eurostat's short-term European economic indicator datasets, covering GDP, inflation, employment, unemployment, business activity, and other economic measures. returned_title: Eurostat – Harmonised Consumer Prices, Monthly Inflation Rates of Change

returned_title: World Bank – Western Balkans Economic Developments and Outlook, Autumn 2026

returned_title: ACLED – Armed Conflict Location & Event Data

It covers television, radio, streaming, online media, and other media formats among German-speaking residents aged 14 and older. Based on a representative survey of 2,500 respondents, it is particularly valuable for analyzing media consumption patterns, demographic differences, and the transition from traditional to digital media.

returned_title: ARD/ZDF Media Study 2025
justification: An annual study documenting media consumption trends in Germany. It examines television, audio, online video, streaming services, and social media. Its findings enable comparisons between traditional and digital media consumption during the 2020s. The study website provides access to published results and supporting data.

returned_title: ARD/ZDF Mass Communication Longitudinal Study 2020
justification: A longitudinal research series measuring media consumption and perceptions in Germany, including a major survey conducted in 2020. It provides historical comparisons of television, radio, newspapers, and internet usage. Particularly useful for investigating how German media consumption evolved entering the 2020s.

returned_title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026 – Germany
justification: Country-specific survey data examining news consumption in Germany in 2026. Includes indicators of trust in news, digital subscriptions, news avoidance, social media news consumption, and the reach of news organizations. Particularly useful for studying recent changes in German journalism and digital news audiences.

returned_title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2025 – Germany
justification: Provides survey-based statistics on German news consumption in 2025. Covers news sources, trust in journalism, online subscriptions, social media, and audience behavior. Enables comparisons across years and countries, making it suitable for research on changing news consumption and digital transformation.

returned_title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2024 – Germany
justification: Contains quantitative indicators of media consumption and attitudes toward journalism in Germany during 2024. Particularly relevant for examining trust in news, digital news subscriptions, traditional versus online news sources, and public attitudes toward artificial intelligence in journalism.

returned_title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2020 – Germany
justification: Provides survey data on German news consumption at the beginning of the 2020s. Includes statistics on television, online news, social media, news brands, digital subscriptions, and trust in journalism. Particularly valuable for establishing a baseline and investigating media consumption during the early COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: German Media Diversity Monitor (Medienvielfaltsmonitor), 2020–2024
justification: An official German media monitoring initiative documenting media diversity, ownership, audience reach, and influence on public opinion. Provides historical results covering multiple years of the 2020s, including 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024. Particularly useful for researching media concentration, market power, and the diversity of news and information sources in Germany.

returned_title: ARD Media Data – Media Usage Statistics in Germany (ARD-Mediendaten)
justification: A statistical resource maintained by German public broadcasting researchers. Provides media-related indicators covering the German television, radio, and digital media landscape. Useful for examining media audiences, consumption trends, and developments in the German media market throughout the 2020s.

returned_title: ARD Media Consumption Statistics (Mediennutzung)
justification: Provides statistical time series on media consumption in Germany, including observations from 2020 onward. The indicators cover the reach and consumption of different media formats. Particularly relevant for comparing changes in German media habits before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: Media Perspektiven – Audio Media Statistics Archive
justification: An archive of statistical data concerning radio, audio streaming, and other forms of audio media consumption in Germany. Includes historical data and statistical publications covering the 2020s. Useful for investigating the changing relationship between traditional radio, digital audio, and internet-based listening.

returned_title: GESIS Survey Dataset on Disinformation and Media Perceptions in Germany
justification: A social science survey dataset examining perceptions of disinformation in Germany. Covers misinformation exposure, social media, journalists, media credibility, online information sources, and public responses to false information. Particularly relevant for research on media trust, misinformation, and the role of digital platforms in German society during the 2020s.

returned_title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2024 – Data and Resources
justification: Provides access to supporting resources for the 2024 Digital News Report, including reusable data visualizations and research materials. The report includes Germany among its surveyed markets. Useful for comparative analysis of German news consumption, media trust, digital subscriptions, and online news behavior.

returned_title: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2025 – Country and Market Data
justification: A collection of country-level news consumption statistics from the 2025 Reuters Institute survey, including Germany. Provides comparable indicators across national media markets. Useful for studying how German news consumption, journalism trust, and digital media adoption compare with other countries.

returned_title: GESIS Data Catalogue – German Media and Communication Research
justification: A research data catalogue maintained by the Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences. Provides access to German survey datasets covering media use, communication, political information, public opinion, and digital behavior. Particularly useful for locating downloadable microdata from surveys conducted between 2020 and 2026. This is a dataset discovery portal rather than a single dataset.

returned_title: RISC Regional Panel 2021–2023: Social Cohesion in Urban and Rural Communities in Germany
justification: Highly relevant dataset examining community life, social cohesion, neighborhood relationships, local infrastructure, media consumption, and social polarization in Germany during 2021–2023. Covers 12 municipalities across Bavaria, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia, and Saxony-Anhalt. Includes large cities, medium-sized towns, and small rural communities, enabling direct comparisons between urban and rural experiences. Particularly useful for investigating local identity, community integration, and differences in everyday social life.

returned_title: German Social Cohesion Panel 2021–2023: Waves 1–3
justification: Longitudinal household survey examining social cohesion, social inequalities, interpersonal relationships, social conflict, and community participation in Germany. Covers the early 2020s and provides repeated observations of individuals and households. Useful for studying changing social relationships, community belonging, social trust, and the effects of socioeconomic differences on everyday life.

returned_title: INKAR: Indicators and Maps for Spatial and Urban Development in Germany, 2021–2025
justification: Comprehensive regional statistical database maintained by Germany's Federal Institute for Research on Building, Urban Affairs and Spatial Development (BBSR). Provides downloadable datasets for 2021, 2022, 2024, and 2025 covering population, housing, employment, education, infrastructure, accessibility, demographics, and regional living conditions. Particularly valuable for comparing quality of life, demographic change, and socioeconomic inequalities between urban and rural areas.

returned_title: Deutschlandatlas: Regional Living Conditions and Urban–Rural Development Indicators
justification: Official German government dataset providing downloadable regional indicators on living conditions, housing, employment, infrastructure, mobility, public services, and demographic development. Includes municipality-level and district-level data, with historical datasets from the 2020s available through its archive. Particularly suitable for identifying geographic inequalities and comparing everyday living conditions across metropolitan, suburban, small-town, and rural communities. Data are available in Excel and CSV formats.

returned_title: Germany 2022 Census: Regional Population, Housing, Households, and Demographic Data
justification: Official nationwide census conducted on May 15, 2022. Provides detailed demographic, household, family, educational, employment, housing, and building statistics at national, state, district, and municipal levels. Particularly useful for examining household composition, urban population density, rural depopulation, housing conditions, family structures, and socioeconomic differences between German communities. Regional tables are downloadable in CSV and Excel formats.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2021–2025
justification: Major representative social survey documenting attitudes, values, social relationships, and social structures among Germany's population. Includes survey waves from 2021, 2023, and 2025. Useful for investigating community belonging, interpersonal trust, social participation, demographic differences, and changing social attitudes during the 2020s. Regional variables in restricted-access versions can support geographic comparisons. Registration is generally required to download the data.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUScompact): Cumulation 1980–2023
justification: Harmonized longitudinal collection of German social survey data, including observations from the early 2020s. Supports analysis of changing community values, social attitudes, interpersonal relationships, socioeconomic circumstances, and demographic characteristics. Particularly useful for comparing social life during the 2020s with earlier decades. Geographic detail is limited in the compact version, making it more suitable for national social trends than detailed urban–rural comparisons.

returned_title: German Regional Atlas: Official Regional Statistics and Geographic Indicators
justification: Official statistical atlas containing more than 100 indicators across German federal states, administrative districts, and urban and rural districts. Covers population, economic activity, education, employment, housing, and other dimensions of regional living conditions. Supports comparisons between cities and rural districts using official statistical data. Underlying indicators can be accessed through Germany's regional statistics database, making this resource useful for quantitative geographic research throughout the 2020s.

returned_title: German Municipal Directory: Population, Area, and Urban–Rural Classification
justification: Official dataset identifying German municipalities and their administrative characteristics, population, geographic area, and regional classifications. Includes information supporting the classification of municipalities by degree of urbanization. Particularly useful for distinguishing urban, suburban, and rural settlements and linking community-level socioeconomic datasets through official geographic identifiers. Can serve as a geographic reference dataset for analyses of German communities during the 2020s.

returned_title: 2022 German Census Database: Municipal and District-Level Community Statistics
justification: Interactive database providing detailed results from Germany's 2022 census. Allows researchers to combine demographic, housing, household, and employment characteristics across municipalities and districts. Particularly useful for examining population composition, settlement patterns, residential circumstances, household structures, and urban–rural demographic differences. Supports customized statistical queries and programmatic access through an API.

returned_title: RISC Research Data Portal: German Social Cohesion and Community Research Datasets
justification: Research data portal containing quantitative and qualitative datasets on social cohesion and community life in Germany. Includes a representative national household panel, a regional panel comparing large cities, medium-sized cities, and rural communities, and qualitative interviews examining experiences across different German regions. Particularly relevant for researching neighborhood relationships, belonging, social infrastructure, local identity, and differences between urban and rural social environments during the 2020s.

returned_title: FULFILL Germany Survey 2023: Quality of Life, Sustainable Lifestyles, and Well-Being
justification: Survey dataset collected in Germany in 2023 as part of the FULFILL research project. Examines lifestyle choices, sustainability, well-being, financial security, environmental quality, health, and perceptions of comfort. Relevant for investigating how everyday living conditions and consumption practices relate to quality of life in contemporary German society. Can complement regional urban–rural datasets when examining sustainable lifestyles and community well-being.

returned_title: Social Cohesion in Times of Crisis: The Corona Pandemic and Anti-Asian Racism in Germany, 2024
justification: Research dataset from the German Center for Integration and Migration Research examining social cohesion, discrimination, and experiences of anti-Asian racism during the COVID-19 pandemic. Relevant for studying minority community experiences, social inclusion, discrimination, and changes in interpersonal relations in Germany during the early 2020s. Particularly valuable for research on how crises affect community belonging and social relationships. Access conditions apply.

returned_title: Deutschlandatlas Historical Regional Data Archive, 2020–2026
justification: Archive of historical German regional development datasets, including multiple releases from 2020 onward. Provides earlier versions of indicators describing demographic conditions, infrastructure, economic opportunities, mobility, housing, and regional quality of life. Particularly useful for tracing changes in urban and rural communities throughout the 2020s rather than relying exclusively on a single cross-sectional dataset. Archived data allow researchers to examine regional development across multiple reference years.

returned_title: Destatis Open Data: Regional Geographic Data and Statistical Maps
justification: Official German statistical open-data resource offering regional geographic boundaries and associated statistical indicators. Regional Atlas geographic data can be downloaded as GeoJSON or Shapefiles, while statistical data are available in CSV and other machine-readable formats. Particularly useful for mapping urban–rural differences, analyzing spatial inequalities, and combining community-level indicators with geographic information systems. Supports spatial research on German settlement patterns and regional living conditions during the 2020s.

returned_title: Destatis – German Tourism Statistics (2020–2026)
justification: Official German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis) data covering tourism, accommodation establishments, overnight stays, and hospitality activities. Includes statistics from the 2020s, making it useful for studying tourism trends in Germany, including the effects of COVID-19 and subsequent recovery.

returned_title: Eurostat – Nights Spent at Tourist Accommodation Establishments
justification: Provides annual statistics on overnight stays in hotels, holiday accommodation, and campsites across European countries, including Germany. Covers 2020–2025 and allows comparisons between domestic and international tourism, accommodation categories, and changes in tourism demand.

returned_title: Eurostat – Monthly Nights Spent at Tourist Accommodation Establishments
justification: Monthly tourism accommodation statistics for Germany during the 2020s. Particularly useful for analyzing seasonal tourism patterns, pandemic-related disruptions, recovery trends, and differences between domestic and foreign visitors.

returned_title: Destatis – Time Use Survey 2022: Leisure Activities by Sex
justification: Official dataset based on Germany's 2022 Time Use Survey. Provides information about time spent on leisure activities among individuals aged 10 and older, with breakdowns by sex. Relevant for studying leisure behavior, recreation, and demographic differences in Germany during the 2020s.

returned_title: Destatis – German Time Use Survey 2022
justification: Comprehensive survey measuring how people in Germany allocate their daily time to different activities, including leisure, recreation, media consumption, and other personal activities. The 2022 survey provides detailed evidence about leisure habits and work-life balance during the 2020s.

returned_title: OECD – Time Use Database
justification: Internationally comparable time-use statistics covering leisure, personal care, paid work, and unpaid work. Includes updated German data from 2022, allowing researchers to compare leisure time in Germany with other OECD countries during the 2020s.

returned_title: German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) – Annual Sports Club Membership Statistics (2020–2026)
justification: Official annual statistics from the German Olympic Sports Confederation covering organized sports participation through club membership registrations. Provides information on sports associations, membership numbers, and regional distribution. Includes annual reports from 2020 through 2026, making it particularly valuable for analyzing sports participation trends before, during, and after the pandemic. Membership counts represent registrations rather than unique individuals.

returned_title: German Olympic Sports Confederation – Sports Club Membership Survey 2024
justification: The 2024 edition of the DOSB annual membership survey provides detailed statistics on organized sport in Germany, including sports federations, clubs, membership categories, and regional differences. Useful for examining participation in different sports and changes in organized recreational activities during the 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Tourism Trips by Detailed Country or World Region of Main Destination
justification: Eurostat dataset measuring tourism trips by destination country and world region. Includes data relevant to German residents' travel behavior during the 2020s. Useful for examining domestic versus international travel patterns, holiday destinations, and changes in tourism preferences.

returned_title: Eurostat – Tourism Trips of EU Residents: Annual Statistics
justification: Official Eurostat tourism survey data covering travel participation, trip duration, purpose, destination, and expenditure. Includes German tourism statistics for the 2020s. Particularly relevant for studying holiday travel, leisure tourism, and changes in travel behavior following COVID-19. The linked page provides dataset documentation and access information.

returned_title: Eurostat – Tourism Trips by EU Residents (Annual Data)
justification: Annual dataset measuring the number of tourism trips taken by residents of European countries, including Germany. Includes personal tourism and travel-related breakdowns. Suitable for analyzing domestic and outbound leisure travel trends during the 2020s and comparing Germany with other European countries.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Camping Sites and Camping Capacity by German Federal State
justification: Official German statistical dataset covering the number of operating campsites, available camping pitches, and occupancy indicators across Germany's federal states. Includes annual observations from 2020 through 2025. Particularly useful for researching outdoor recreation, camping tourism, regional tourism infrastructure, and leisure travel trends.

returned_title: Statistikportal – Tourism Statistics by German Federal State
justification: Regional tourism statistics published through Germany's official statistical portal. Includes data on tourist arrivals, overnight stays, and accommodation activities across German federal states, with observations covering the 2020s. Valuable for comparing tourism development between regions and identifying geographical differences in leisure travel.

returned_title: Destatis – Overnight Stays in Germany: Short-Term Tourism Indicators
justification: Official short-term statistics tracking overnight stays in Germany's tourism accommodation sector. Provides observations during the 2020s and supports analysis of tourism growth, seasonal patterns, and fluctuations in visitor activity. Particularly relevant for monitoring tourism recovery and recent changes in accommodation demand.

returned_title: Eurostat – German Time Use Survey 2022: National Metadata
justification: Official documentation for Germany's 2022 Time Use Survey, conducted between January and December 2022. Describes the survey methodology, population coverage, and availability of microdata through research data centers. Relevant for researchers seeking detailed individual-level information about leisure, physical activity, and recreational behavior. This is a metadata and access-information page rather than a direct microdata download.

returned_title: Eurostat – Tourism Participation and Accommodation Data
justification: Official Eurostat tourism data portal providing access to datasets on tourism participation, travel expenditure, trips, overnight stays, and accommodation establishments. Includes German observations covering the 2020s. Particularly useful for locating multiple harmonized datasets and comparing Germany's tourism sector with other European countries.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2023 – Religion and Worldview
justification: One of the most directly relevant datasets for studying religion and values in Germany during the 2020s. The 2023 survey specifically focuses on religion and worldview (Religion und Weltanschauung). It includes religious affiliation, church attendance, prayer, belief in God, spirituality, religious fundamentalism, attitudes toward other religions, moral values, tolerance, and individual value orientations. It also covers postmaterialism, traditional values, and attitudes toward social issues. Particularly useful for examining relationships between religiosity, secularization, and social values in contemporary Germany.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2021
justification: A nationally representative survey of the German population conducted in 2021. ALLBUS provides information about religious affiliation, religious practices, social attitudes, political orientations, and demographic characteristics. The 2021 dataset is useful for investigating religious identities and value orientations during the COVID-19 pandemic and comparing them with subsequent survey waves. Data are available through GESIS, with registration required for downloading.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2025
justification: A recent wave of Germany's long-running General Social Survey. ALLBUS 2025 provides updated information on German society, including social attitudes and demographic characteristics. It can be combined with the 2021 and 2023 waves to investigate changes in religious affiliation, values, and social attitudes throughout the 2020s. The GESIS documentation provides access to available datasets and questionnaires.

returned_title: ALLBUS 2023 Supplementary Dataset – Measuring Religious Fundamentalism
justification: A specialized supplementary dataset associated with ALLBUS 2023, identified as GESIS study ZA8836. It focuses on measuring religious fundamentalism in Germany. Particularly relevant for research examining religious conservatism, fundamentalist beliefs, religious identity, and their relationships with broader social values. It can complement the main ALLBUS 2023 religion and worldview dataset.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) Round 11 – Germany, 2023–2024
justification: A major comparative European survey containing German data collected during 2023–2024. It includes measures of religious affiliation, religiosity, religious attendance, social trust, political attitudes, national identity, perceived discrimination, and human values. The Human Values Scale measures orientations such as tradition, conformity, universalism, benevolence, and self-direction. Germany can be selected in the ESS data portal, making this dataset especially useful for comparing religious and secular value orientations across European societies.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) Round 10 – Germany, 2020–2022
justification: A cross-national survey wave covering the early 2020s. It contains standardized indicators of religious affiliation, religious attendance, subjective religiosity, political attitudes, social trust, and human values. German observations can be selected through the ESS Data Portal. Particularly useful for examining religion and values during the pandemic period and comparing German respondents with those in other European countries. The ESS Human Values Scale supports detailed analysis of traditional, secular, and universalist orientations.

returned_title: Sixth Church Membership Survey (KMU 6) – Germany, 2022–2023
justification: A major German study examining religion, church membership, religiosity, spirituality, and the societal role of religious institutions. The sixth Kirchenmitgliedschaftsuntersuchung surveyed 5,282 respondents and published its initial findings in 2023. It covers religious orientations, relationships with churches, trust in religious institutions, secularization, social background, and expectations concerning religious organizations. Particularly valuable because it includes both religiously affiliated and unaffiliated individuals. The landing page provides extensive survey findings and documentation, although access to respondent-level microdata is not established.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) Wave 7 – 2017–2022
justification: An international survey dataset examining religion, morality, cultural values, social trust, political beliefs, and attitudes toward democracy. It includes indicators of religious importance, belief in God, religious participation, tolerance, family values, and moral judgments. The survey period overlaps with the early 2020s. Researchers should check the country documentation for the exact German fieldwork dates before treating observations as evidence specifically from the 2020s. Useful for international comparisons and studying relationships between religion and broader cultural orientations.

returned_title: Joint European Values Study / World Values Survey (EVS/WVS) 2017–2022
justification: A harmonized international dataset combining the European Values Study and World Values Survey. It includes more than 156,000 respondents across 92 countries and regions, including Germany, with interviews conducted between 2017 and 2022. Variables cover religious beliefs, religious participation, traditional versus secular values, family norms, morality, social trust, and political attitudes. Particularly useful for comparing German value orientations with those in other countries and examining the relationship between religion and cultural change. Country-specific fieldwork dates should be checked when restricting analysis to the 2020s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) 2022 – Family and Changing Gender Roles V
justification: A comparative survey dataset with German interviews conducted between May and August 2023. It focuses on family values, gender roles, marriage, parenting, household responsibilities, and attitudes toward alternative family arrangements. The data can help investigate the relationship between religious affiliation and traditional or progressive social values. Particularly relevant for examining how religious identity intersects with attitudes toward gender equality, marriage, and family structures in contemporary Germany.

returned_title: ISSP Family and Changing Gender Roles I–V – Cumulated Dataset, 1988–2022
justification: A harmonized longitudinal collection of ISSP surveys examining family and gender values across several decades, including the 2022 module with German observations collected in 2023. It supports analysis of changing attitudes toward marriage, parenting, women's employment, gender equality, and family responsibilities. Particularly useful for assessing whether traditional values associated with religious orientations have declined or persisted in Germany over time.

returned_title: ALLBUS Cumulation 1980–2023 – German General Social Survey
justification: A cumulative dataset combining multiple waves of the German General Social Survey, including observations from the 2020s. It allows researchers to trace long-term developments in religious affiliation, church attendance, social values, moral attitudes, political orientations, and demographic characteristics. Particularly valuable for analyzing secularization, generational differences, and the evolution of religious and nonreligious values in Germany. The cumulative design makes it possible to place changes observed during the 2020s in a broader historical context.

returned_title: Ecumenical Church Atlas (Ökumenischer Kirchenatlas) – Germany
justification: An open-data resource providing geographical and statistical information about Christian churches in Germany. It draws on administrative church records and presents information on religious institutions and church membership. Particularly useful for examining regional differences in Christian affiliation and institutional religious presence. It can complement individual-level surveys such as ALLBUS and ESS by providing contextual information about religion across German regions. Its primary focus is church statistics rather than individual moral or cultural values.

returned_title: Longitudinal Mental Health Data Collected via the Corona Health Smartphone App During COVID-19 (2020–2025)
justification: An open-access psychological health dataset collected in Germany between July 2020 and January 2025. Contains baseline assessments from 2,704 adults and 11,541 repeated assessments. Covers psychological well-being, quality of life, coping mechanisms, pandemic-related concerns, and behavioral patterns. Includes downloadable CSV files and a codebook. Particularly useful for longitudinal research on psychological changes during the 2020s.

returned_title: Mental Health of Adolescents During COVID-19 – Corona Health Project
justification: An openly available dataset published in 2025 by researchers at the University of Würzburg. Investigates adolescent mental health and behavioral changes during the COVID-19 pandemic. Includes baseline and follow-up questionnaires, demographic information, and, where consent was provided, location and digital behavioral data. Relevant for developmental psychology, adolescent mental health, and pandemic-related psychological research in Germany.

returned_title: Recognizing and Understanding Stress in Adults During COVID-19 – Corona Health App
justification: A psychological stress dataset collected through the Corona Health smartphone application developed in collaboration with Germany's Robert Koch Institute. Contains longitudinal assessments collected between December 2020 and May 2025. Suitable for studying stress, psychological responses, and factors associated with adult mental health during and after the pandemic. The underlying research data are available through Zenodo.

returned_title: Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), Version 42 – Germany, 1984–2025
justification: A major representative longitudinal household dataset maintained by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin). Its coverage includes the entire 2020–2025 period. Contains information relevant to psychology, including subjective well-being, health, life satisfaction, and social circumstances. Particularly valuable for investigating relationships between psychological well-being, employment, socioeconomic conditions, and major societal changes. Access to the remote edition is subject to research data access arrangements.

returned_title: Mental Health in Germany Before, During and After the COVID-19 Pandemic – Replication Dataset
justification: A research replication dataset associated with an investigation of psychological health in Germany using nationally representative Panel Study Labour Market and Social Security (PASS) observations from 2018 to 2022. The research examines changes in mental health before, during, and after the pandemic, including differences across socioeconomic groups. Useful for reproducing statistical analyses and investigating psychological health inequalities. The repository contains replication material rather than necessarily providing unrestricted access to the underlying individual-level PASS data.

returned_title: FReDA – The German Family Demography Panel
justification: A German longitudinal population survey beginning in 2021, archived through GESIS. Contains information about family relationships, partnerships, household circumstances, and related social and personal experiences. Relevant for family psychology, relationship psychology, subjective well-being, and the psychological consequences of changing family structures. Includes multiple survey waves throughout the 2020s, allowing researchers to investigate changes over time.

returned_title: The German Family Panel (pairfam) – Release 14.2
justification: A longitudinal German dataset examining intimate relationships, family development, and interpersonal dynamics. Its later survey waves cover the early 2020s, and Release 14.2 was published in 2024. Particularly relevant to relationship psychology, attachment, family functioning, emotional well-being, and developmental psychology. Scientific-use data are available to eligible researchers through GESIS.

returned_title: Panel Study Labour Market and Social Security (PASS) – Version 0622
justification: A German longitudinal dataset maintained by the Institute for Employment Research (IAB). Includes survey information relevant to psychological health, socioeconomic stress, employment, and social inequalities. Its observations extend into the 2020s, making it suitable for investigating the psychological consequences of unemployment, financial insecurity, and changing living conditions. Access to detailed microdata is regulated by the research data center.

returned_title: Longitudinal Development of Depression and Anxiety During COVID-19 in Germany – Population-Based Probability Sample
justification: A 2022 research publication describing a longitudinal psychological survey of German adults conducted in May and November 2020. The first assessment included 1,412 respondents, while the second included 743. Focuses specifically on depressive symptoms and anxiety. Relevant for clinical psychology, psychiatric epidemiology, and population mental health research. The DOI leads to the research publication describing the underlying survey; it is not a dedicated dataset download page.

returned_title: Mental Health Across Two Years of the COVID-19 Pandemic – Five-Wave Longitudinal Study in Germany
justification: A German longitudinal psychological study covering May 2020 through April 2022. Includes five assessment waves involving 636 adults from the general population. Investigates changes in psychological health throughout different stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. Particularly relevant for studying mental health trajectories, psychological distress, and individual differences in responses to prolonged societal stress. The DOI identifies the study publication rather than an independently verified public dataset repository.

returned_title: One Year After the COVID-19 Outbreak in Germany – Longitudinal Mental Health Survey
justification: A longitudinal psychological study based on 1,388 adults in Germany initially assessed between April and May 2020, with follow-up measurements after six and twelve months. Examines depression, anxiety, loneliness, psychological distress, and life satisfaction. Particularly relevant for understanding changes in mental health during the first year of the pandemic and identifying psychologically vulnerable populations. The DOI links to the research article, and access to its underlying participant-level data is not established by this record.

returned_title: Health Behaviors and Mental Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic – Longitudinal Population-Based Survey in Germany
justification: A longitudinal German population survey conducted during the first months of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, involving approximately 3,500 randomly selected participants. Measures anxiety, depression, loneliness, physical activity, screen time, and eating behaviors. Particularly useful for health psychology, behavioral psychology, and research examining associations between lifestyle behaviors and mental health. The DOI identifies the research publication rather than a verified standalone dataset.

returned_title: Longitudinal Changes in Anxiety and Psychological Distress During the First Three Months of COVID-19 in Germany
justification: A German longitudinal psychological survey conducted across four waves between March 27 and June 15, 2020. Examines anxiety, psychological distress, and associated risk and protective factors. Relevant for clinical psychology, stress research, and the psychological consequences of public health emergencies. The survey uses a convenience sample, which should be considered when interpreting population-level findings. The DOI links to the study publication, not a confirmed downloadable dataset.

returned_title: Psychological Burden Over 1.5 Years of the COVID-19 Pandemic in Germany – Nine-Wave Longitudinal Community Study
justification: A German longitudinal psychological investigation covering nine survey waves from March 2020 through October 2021. Examines psychological burden and changes in mental health across different pandemic phases. Particularly relevant for longitudinal clinical psychology, psychological stress, and understanding adaptation to prolonged uncertainty. The linked landing page provides the research article and study methodology; unrestricted access to the underlying participant-level dataset is not confirmed.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2023
justification: A major representative survey examining social attitudes, behaviours, values, and societal change in Germany. Covers political opinions, social inequality, religion, trust, social relationships, and demographic characteristics. Particularly relevant for studying German society in the 2020s and comparing contemporary attitudes with historical trends.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Data and Documentation, 2021–2025
justification: Provides access to multiple waves of Germany's long-running general social survey, including surveys conducted during the 2020s. Covers social values, interpersonal trust, political participation, social integration, attitudes toward immigration, and social inequality. Especially useful for analysing changes in social behaviour and attitudes across different years.

returned_title: Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2025
justification: A nationally representative longitudinal household panel conducted annually in Germany. Contains observations from 2020–2025 covering social relationships, subjective well-being, life satisfaction, economic insecurity, employment, family dynamics, and social attitudes. Particularly valuable for tracking how individual behaviours and attitudes evolved throughout the decade.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS), Round 10 (2020–2022)
justification: A cross-national survey containing German respondents and extensive measures of social attitudes, political trust, democratic values, social participation, discrimination, and well-being. Round 10 includes modules on democracy and digital social contacts, making it useful for investigating social interactions and attitudes during the early 2020s.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS), Round 11 (2023–2024)
justification: Provides internationally comparable survey data on social attitudes and behaviours, including Germany. Covers interpersonal trust, institutional confidence, political participation, social inequality, gender attitudes, health inequalities, discrimination, and subjective well-being. Particularly valuable for examining contemporary German social attitudes in a comparative European context.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES), 2021–2025
justification: A comprehensive collection of longitudinal and cross-sectional datasets examining political and social attitudes in Germany. Includes survey data surrounding the 2021 and 2025 federal elections, covering political trust, democratic satisfaction, ideological orientations, electoral participation, political engagement, and attitudes toward public policy. Useful for understanding social and political behaviour during the 2020s.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES), Cross-Section 2025, Post-Election
justification: A survey of people in Germany conducted between February and April 2025, containing 7,336 observations and 611 variables. Examines political behaviour, attitudes, electoral participation, and perceptions of political institutions. Particularly relevant for analysing recent social divisions, political preferences, and democratic engagement in Germany.

Particularly useful for studying economic disparities between eastern and western Germany, regional industrial concentration, urban economic development, and geographical differences in economic performance during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Regional Economic Accounts
justification: Regional economic accounts covering GDP, gross value added, employment, and capital formation across European regions, including Germany. Data extend from 2000 into the 2020s, enabling comparisons across both decades. Useful for analyzing regional economic development, differences in productivity, industrial restructuring, and uneven economic growth.

returned_title: Eurostat – German Regional Economic Accounts
justification: Germany-specific documentation and statistical coverage of regional economic accounts, including GDP, gross value added by industry, employment, and investment-related indicators. Relevant for investigating structural differences between German federal states, regional economic specialization, and long-term development patterns. Particularly valuable for studies of regional convergence and persistent economic disparities.

returned_title: Destatis – Short-Term Economic Indicators
justification: Official German economic time-series resource providing monthly and quarterly indicators related to industrial production, employment, and other aspects of economic activity. Useful for analyzing business cycles, economic fluctuations, and Germany's economic response to major disruptions during the 2010s and 2020s. Historical data remain available, although the standalone short-term indicators service was scheduled for discontinuation in October 2026, with the underlying statistics accessible through GENESIS-Online.

returned_title: Eurostat – National Accounts Data and Methodology
justification: Official Eurostat resource explaining and providing access to harmonized national accounts datasets based on the European System of Accounts 2010 framework. Relevant for examining Germany's GDP, employment, investment, government activity, and sectoral development. Particularly valuable for ensuring methodological consistency when comparing German economic indicators across the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: World Bank – Germany Gross National Savings
justification: Germany-specific World Bank time series focusing on gross national savings. Useful for studying capital accumulation, savings behavior, investment capacity, and macroeconomic development throughout the 2010s and 2020s. Can support research into Germany's export-oriented economic model, domestic investment patterns, and relationships between national savings and economic growth.

returned_title: OECD Main Science and Technology Indicators (MSTI)
justification: One of the most comprehensive datasets for studying science and technology in Germany during the 2010s and 2020s. Contains approximately 148 indicators covering research and development (R&D) expenditure, research personnel, government R&D budgets, patents, and international trade in R&D-intensive industries. Provides longitudinal data suitable for analyzing Germany's scientific and technological development and comparing its performance with other OECD countries.

returned_title: Eurostat: Gross Domestic Expenditure on R&D by Sector of Performance and Source of Funds
justification: Official European statistical dataset covering R&D expenditure in Germany from 1980 to 2024. Includes annual spending by businesses, government institutions, higher education institutions, and other sectors, classified by funding source. Particularly useful for investigating changes in German research investment between 2010 and 2024, including public-private funding patterns and R&D expenditure as a percentage of GDP.

returned_title: German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis): Research and Development Expenditure by Sector
justification: Official German government statistics detailing annual research and development expenditure across government institutions, universities, and private enterprises. The published table covers 2014–2024 and reports spending in millions of euros. Particularly relevant for examining Germany's domestic R&D investment trends, including changes during the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent recovery.

returned_title: German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space: Expenditure on Science, Research and Development
justification: Official German federal research statistics portal providing datasets on science and technology financing. Includes research expenditure across institutional sectors and regional distributions among Germany's federal states (Länder). Useful for examining changes in science funding during the 2010s and 2020s, identifying regional differences in research investment, and evaluating Germany's national research priorities.

returned_title: OECD Science, Technology and Innovation Scoreboard
justification: Comprehensive international database containing more than 1,000 indicators related to scientific research, technological innovation, patents, education, business innovation, and economic performance. Includes Germany and allows cross-country comparisons and analysis of historical trends. Especially valuable for studying Germany's technological competitiveness, innovation ecosystem, and scientific capabilities throughout the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: European Innovation Scoreboard 2026: EU Countries and Neighbouring Countries Database
justification: European Commission dataset assessing innovation performance across EU member states, including Germany. The 2026 edition provides downloadable country-level data covering 32 indicators across four major innovation dimensions. Includes measures of research systems, human resources, innovation investment, intellectual assets, and economic impacts. Useful for comparing Germany's innovation performance with other European countries and examining historical developments.

returned_title: European Commission Regional Innovation Scoreboard
justification: Regional innovation dataset covering European regions, including Germany's federal states and subnational regions. The 2025 edition includes 23 innovation indicators and provides historical comparisons, while earlier editions are available for 2012, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2021, and 2023. Particularly useful for examining regional disparities in German scientific and technological innovation, identifying research-intensive regions, and tracking changes over time.

returned_title: Eurostat: R&D Personnel by Sector of Performance, Professional Position and Sex
justification: European statistical dataset providing information on research and development personnel, including researchers and other R&D staff, categorized by institutional sector, professional position, and sex. Historical data include the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly relevant for analyzing Germany's scientific workforce, the expansion of research employment, gender representation in research, and changes in the distribution of researchers between universities, businesses, and government institutions.

returned_title: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO): Intellectual Property Statistics
justification: Official international intellectual property statistics providing patent, trademark, and industrial design indicators for Germany and other countries. Includes information on patent applications, patents in force, technological fields, and international intellectual property activity. Suitable for examining German technological invention and patenting trends during the 2010s and 2020s, particularly in engineering, manufacturing, and emerging technologies.

returned_title: Eurostat: Community Innovation Survey (CIS) Statistics
justification: Harmonized European business innovation statistics covering Germany and other EU countries. The Community Innovation Survey measures innovation activities among enterprises, including product innovation, business process innovation, innovation cooperation, and innovation expenditure. Multiple survey waves are available across the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for investigating technological innovation among German businesses, comparing innovation across industries, and studying relationships between R&D investment and commercial innovation.

returned_title: Eurostat: Households – Level of Internet Access
justification: Annual European dataset measuring household internet access, including Germany, from 2002 to 2025. Provides a consistent indicator of digital technology adoption across the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for evaluating Germany's digital transformation, identifying long-term changes in household connectivity, and comparing Germany's digital infrastructure adoption with other European countries.

returned_title: Eurostat: Regional Household Internet Access
justification: Regional dataset measuring the percentage of households with internet access across European regions, including German regions, between 2006 and 2025. Particularly useful for analyzing geographic disparities in digital technology adoption within Germany, comparing urban and regional digital development, and studying how household connectivity evolved during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat: Households – Type of Connection to the Internet (2003–2021)
justification: Historical dataset describing household internet connection technologies, including broadband and other connection types, across European countries including Germany. Covers 2003–2021, making it particularly relevant for analyzing technological transitions during the 2010s and early 2020s. Useful for investigating Germany's adoption of broadband connectivity and the evolution of digital communications infrastructure.

returned_title: Eurostat: ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals – Research Microdata
justification: European survey microdata covering information and communication technology adoption and usage, including Germany. The underlying annual surveys provide information on internet use, digital activities, online services, electronic commerce, and individual characteristics. Particularly valuable for detailed research into Germany's digital society during the 2010s and 2020s. Access to scientific-use microdata may require an application and approval.

returned_title: German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis): Research and Development Statistics
justification: Official German statistical portal providing datasets and tables on domestic R&D expenditure, research personnel, and research activities across institutional sectors. Includes historical statistical series suitable for examining developments in German science and technology during the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful as a primary national source for validating international statistics and investigating Germany-specific research trends.

returned_title: Eurostat: Total Intramural R&D Expenditure by Sector of Performance and Fields of Science
justification: Historical European R&D expenditure dataset covering research spending by scientific field and performing sector, including Germany. The archived dataset provides observations extending through 2014, making it especially useful for studying the early 2010s. It supports analysis of how German research expenditure was distributed across scientific disciplines and institutional sectors.

returned_title: Eurostat: Enterprises by Main Types of Innovation, Economic Activity and Size Class
justification: Historical Community Innovation Survey dataset describing enterprise innovation activities by industry and business size, including German companies. Particularly useful for studying the structure of German technological innovation during the early 2010s and comparing innovation patterns between small, medium-sized, and large enterprises. Provides a historical complement to more recent European innovation surveys.

returned_title: German Federal Statistical Office Research and Development Indicators – DESTATIS Dataset 21821BJ001
justification: Structured time-series dataset derived from Germany's Federal Statistical Office and distributed through DBnomics. Includes annual German R&D expenditure, R&D expenditure as a percentage of GDP, expenditure per employed person, and R&D personnel measured in full-time equivalents. Covers 1995–2024, providing consistent historical observations for both the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly suitable for quantitative analysis, visualization, and statistical modeling of Germany's science and technology investment.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core) – Longitudinal Household and Individual Data
justification: One of Germany's most comprehensive longitudinal datasets for studying economic inequality, poverty, social mobility, and social exclusion. The dataset covers 1984–2021, including the 2010s and early 2020s. It provides individual- and household-level information on income, employment, education, housing, health, migration, and subjective well-being. Particularly useful for investigating changes in inequality over time, differences between eastern and western Germany, and disparities across demographic groups.

returned_title: European Union Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC) – Germany
justification: A major source of harmonized microdata on income inequality, poverty, material deprivation, housing conditions, and social exclusion. Germany has participated since 2005, making the dataset particularly suitable for examining developments throughout the 2010s and 2020s. It provides cross-sectional and longitudinal data and enables comparisons between Germany and other European countries. Researchers can investigate poverty risks by age, gender, education, employment status, and household composition. Access to research microdata requires authorization.

returned_title: Eurostat – Persons at Risk of Poverty or Social Exclusion by Age and Sex (ilc_peps01n)
justification: An official statistical dataset measuring the proportion of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion in Germany and other European countries. It provides annual observations covering the 2010s and 2020s, with breakdowns by age and gender. The indicator combines income poverty, severe material and social deprivation, and very low work intensity. Particularly relevant for identifying vulnerable population groups and assessing changes in social exclusion. Changes to indicator definitions and survey methodology should be considered when comparing years.

returned_title: Eurostat – Gini Coefficient of Equivalised Disposable Income (ilc_di12)
justification: An official annual dataset measuring income inequality through the Gini coefficient. It includes Germany and other European countries, allowing analysis of income distribution during the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly suitable for examining whether income inequality increased or decreased, comparing Germany with European averages, and evaluating long-term distributional trends. Data are derived primarily from EU-SILC.

returned_title: Eurostat – Gini Coefficient Before Social Transfers (ilc_di12b)
justification: Provides annual inequality indicators for Germany and other European countries, with coverage extending from 2003 to 2025. Unlike the conventional disposable-income Gini indicator, this dataset measures inequality before social transfers, with pensions included among transfers. Comparing it with post-transfer inequality measures helps investigate the redistributive effects of Germany's welfare system during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – At-Risk-of-Poverty Rate by Poverty Threshold and Economic Activity (ilc_li04)
justification: Contains harmonized poverty indicators that can be used to examine the relationship between employment status and income poverty in Germany. The dataset covers multiple years across the 2010s and 2020s and distinguishes population groups according to their predominant economic activity. Particularly useful for studying in-work poverty, unemployment-related poverty, and economic vulnerability among people outside the labor force.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulated Survey Data
justification: A major repeated cross-sectional survey documenting social attitudes, demographic characteristics, and social structures in Germany. The cumulative datasets include observations from the 2010s and 2020s. Relevant topics include perceptions of social inequality, social class, discrimination, migration, gender roles, political participation, and attitudes toward redistribution and the welfare state. Particularly useful for studying perceived inequality and social exclusion alongside socioeconomic characteristics. Data are available through GESIS, with registration required for downloads.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2021
justification: A specifically identifiable cumulative survey dataset covering Germany from 1980 to 2021. Its thematic classification explicitly includes equality, inequality, and social exclusion. It contains information on social stratification, economic conditions, migration, minority groups, gender roles, and social attitudes. Particularly useful for comparing social inequality and perceptions of exclusion across different survey waves in the 2010s and early 2020s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) 2019 – Social Inequality V
justification: An international survey dataset specifically focused on social inequality, including a German sample of 1,325 respondents interviewed between July and September 2020. It measures attitudes toward income differences, perceptions of social mobility, views on distributive justice, social class identification, and beliefs about opportunities for advancement. Particularly valuable for analyzing subjective perceptions of inequality in Germany and comparing them internationally. Registration is required to download the data.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality Cumulated Data
justification: A harmonized collection of international surveys on social inequality conducted in 1987, 1992, 1999, 2009, and 2019. Germany participated in these survey waves. The series covers perceptions of economic inequality, social stratification, income differences, social conflict, and opportunities for upward mobility. Especially useful for investigating how German attitudes toward inequality evolved before and during the 2010s, with the 2019 module providing observations collected in Germany in 2020.

returned_title: Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Destatis) – Risk of Poverty or Social Exclusion by Age and Gender
justification: Official German statistical tables reporting the population at risk of poverty or social exclusion, disaggregated by age and gender. The published series includes data for 2020–2023, derived from the German EU-SILC component of the Microcensus. Particularly useful for examining gender inequalities, child poverty, and the economic vulnerability of older people. The tables also document the methodological break introduced in 2020, an important consideration when analyzing trends across decades.

returned_title: Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Destatis) – Material Deprivation by Social Status, 2019
justification: An official dataset examining material deprivation among German households in 2019. It distinguishes between employed, unemployed, retired, and economically inactive population groups. Indicators include difficulty paying housing expenses, maintaining adequate indoor temperatures, and meeting essential living costs. Particularly useful for studying economic exclusion and living-standard inequalities immediately before the COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: German Microcensus – Population, Employment, Education, and Living Conditions
justification: Germany's large-scale official household survey provides information relevant to inequality in employment, education, family structures, migration, housing, and economic living conditions. It supports investigations of socioeconomic disparities across population groups and regions during the 2010s and 2020s. Since 2020, EU-SILC has been integrated into the Microcensus. Researchers should account for the 2020 redesign when conducting longitudinal comparisons. The linked page describes the survey and its methodological changes.

returned_title: German EU-SILC (Leben in Europa) – Income and Living Conditions
justification: The German implementation of the European Statistics on Income and Living Conditions survey. It collects information about household income, housing, health, poverty, and other dimensions of living standards. The survey has operated since 2005, providing coverage of the 2010s and 2020s. It is particularly relevant for studying multidimensional poverty and social exclusion in Germany. This official landing page explains the data collection and its role in producing comparable European poverty statistics.

returned_title: Eurostat – EU-SILC Income and Living Conditions Data Collection
justification: An official entry point to annual European income and living-conditions datasets, including data for Germany. It covers income distribution, poverty, social inclusion, material deprivation, and household living conditions. The underlying EU-SILC data include annual indicators and additional thematic modules, allowing researchers to investigate several dimensions of inequality across the 2010s and 2020s. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal data are documented.

returned_title: Federal Employment Agency – Basic Income Support for Jobseekers (SGB II) Statistics
justification: An official German administrative statistics resource related to unemployment assistance, basic income support, and labor-market vulnerability. The linked methodological collection includes historical statistical tables and data covering years in the 2010s, as well as documentation relevant to later reporting. These statistics can help investigate dependence on social assistance, transitions from benefit receipt into employment, and inequalities in labor-market participation. The page is primarily a methodological and historical data entry point rather than a single harmonized dataset.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2023
justification: A nationally representative longitudinal dataset covering Germany throughout the 2010s and early 2020s. Particularly valuable for psychological research on mental health, subjective well-being, life satisfaction, personality, stress, and social relationships. Annual observations allow researchers to investigate psychological changes over time and associations with employment, income, education, and family circumstances. Research access is subject to data-use conditions.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Cumulation 1980–2023
justification: A large-scale German population survey covering social attitudes, values, beliefs, interpersonal trust, social integration, and subjective evaluations of society. Includes multiple survey waves from the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for social psychology, political psychology, attitude formation, and research on psychological differences between population groups. Data are distributed through GESIS.

returned_title: German Family Panel (pairfam), Waves 1–14, 2008–2022
justification: A longitudinal German study focusing on intimate relationships, family dynamics, parenting, and individual development. Covers almost the entire 2010s and the beginning of the 2020s. Particularly relevant to developmental psychology, family psychology, attachment, relationship satisfaction, emotional well-being, and intergenerational relationships. Includes information from respondents and, in various waves, their partners, parents, and children.

returned_title: German Health Update (GEDA), 2010, 2012, 2014/2015, and 2019/2020
justification: A series of nationally representative health surveys conducted by Germany's Robert Koch Institute. Provides information on population health, including indicators relevant to mental health, psychological distress, perceived health, and health-related quality of life. The 2010, 2012, 2014/2015, and 2019/2020 datasets are especially useful for investigating psychological health trends before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Scientific-use files are available through the institute's research data center.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults (DEGS1), 2008–2011
justification: A nationally representative German adult health study containing information relevant to psychological health, mental disorders, depressive symptoms, health behaviors, and psychosocial risk factors. Data collection continued into 2011, making it a useful baseline for psychological research focused on the early 2010s. The dataset supports investigations of associations between mental health, physical health, demographic characteristics, and social conditions.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Children and Adolescents (KiGGS), Waves 1 and 2
justification: A major German population health study covering children and adolescents aged 0–17. Wave 1 was conducted during 2009–2012, with Wave 2 conducted during the 2010s. Particularly relevant for developmental psychology, child and adolescent mental health, emotional and behavioral difficulties, psychosocial development, and family-related influences on psychological well-being. Scientific-use datasets are available through the Robert Koch Institute.

returned_title: German National Cohort (NAKO Gesundheitsstudie)
justification: A large German population-based longitudinal health study that collects psychological, cognitive, behavioral, and mental health information. Its observation period includes the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for investigating depression, psychological distress, cognitive functioning, health-related behaviors, and relationships between mental and physical health. Researchers can request access to study data through the NAKO data access system.

returned_title: Transitions and Old Age Potential (TOP), Waves 1–3
justification: A German longitudinal survey examining individuals approaching or entering retirement, initially focusing on people aged 55–70. Covers multiple observations during the 2010s. Includes information on psychological well-being, attitudes toward aging, life transitions, employment, retirement, and subjective health. Particularly relevant for lifespan developmental psychology, gerontopsychology, retirement adjustment, and psychological adaptation to aging.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Individual Surveys and Historical Cumulations
justification: The official GESIS dataset collection provides individual ALLBUS survey waves from the 2010s and 2020s, alongside cumulative datasets. Individual waves can contain psychological and social-attitudinal measures omitted from cumulative files. Relevant research themes include social identity, prejudice, interpersonal trust, subjective social position, values, and attitudes toward migration. Particularly useful for examining psychological and social changes in Germany across survey years.

returned_title: SOEP-Core v40.1, Updated German Socio-Economic Panel Data, 1984–2023
justification: An updated edition of Germany's major longitudinal household survey, providing observations throughout the 2010s and into the 2020s. Relevant psychological variables include subjective well-being, health, life satisfaction, and individual characteristics associated with psychological development. The dataset is particularly suitable for studying long-term changes in mental health and well-being, including differences across generations and socioeconomic groups. Several access editions are available.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2025
justification: One of the most comprehensive longitudinal datasets for studying social stratification in Germany during the 2010s and 2020s. Conducted annually by DIW Berlin, it covers household income, wealth, education, occupational status, employment, migration background, family structure, and social mobility. Particularly useful for examining class differences, intergenerational inequality, income distribution, and changes in socioeconomic status over time. The dataset includes observations through 2025, with access subject to research data agreements.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Cumulation 1980–2023
justification: A major repeated cross-sectional survey of the German population, administered by GESIS. Particularly relevant for examining subjective social class, occupational prestige, educational attainment, income inequality, social mobility, religious affiliation, and attitudes toward social inequality. The cumulative dataset allows researchers to compare social stratification patterns throughout the 2010s and early 2020s. It also provides information about perceived social standing and attitudes toward redistribution.

returned_title: German Microcensus (Mikrozensus), 2010s–2020s
justification: Germany's largest annual household survey, conducted by the Federal Statistical Office and state statistical offices. It provides detailed information about education, occupational groups, employment, household composition, nationality, migration background, and socioeconomic characteristics. Its large sample makes it especially valuable for analyzing differences between social classes, demographic groups, regions, and migrant populations. Multiple survey years from the 2010s and 2020s are available, although access to detailed microdata is restricted.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS), Scientific Use Files
justification: A large German longitudinal education study that follows individuals across different educational stages and into adulthood. Particularly useful for investigating educational stratification, intergenerational social mobility, family socioeconomic background, and inequalities in educational opportunities. The dataset includes information on parental education, occupational status, migration background, educational achievement, and transitions into employment. Data collected throughout the 2010s and 2020s support research on how social origins influence educational and occupational outcomes.

returned_title: GESIS Panel.pop, 2013–2020s
justification: A longitudinal survey of the German-speaking adult population, established in 2013. It provides repeated observations on socioeconomic characteristics, social attitudes, political preferences, and demographic group membership. Relevant for studying differences between social groups, changes in social identities, perceived inequalities, and socioeconomic influences on attitudes. The dataset contains multiple recruitment cohorts, enabling comparisons across the 2010s and 2020s. Standard scientific datasets are available for secondary research.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP): Social Inequality V, 2019
justification: A comparative international survey that includes Germany and focuses specifically on social inequality and stratification. The 2019 Social Inequality module examines perceptions of income differences, social mobility, occupational prestige, distributive justice, and attitudes toward inequality. It is particularly appropriate for analyzing how different socioeconomic groups perceive Germany's class structure. The GESIS data catalog provides access to the dataset and its documentation.

returned_title: Sample of Integrated Labour Market Biographies (SIAB), 1975–2023
justification: A longitudinal administrative dataset produced by the Institute for Employment Research (IAB), documenting employment histories and labor market trajectories in Germany. It supports analysis of occupational stratification, earnings differences, unemployment, labor market segmentation, and socioeconomic mobility. Particularly valuable for examining inequalities between occupational groups, educational categories, and demographic populations during the 2010s and early 2020s. The linked page describes the 1975–2023 data release; access to individual-level records requires authorization.

returned_title: IAB-SOEP Migration Samples, 2013–2025
justification: A longitudinal survey component of the German Socio-Economic Panel designed to improve the representation of individuals with migration backgrounds. It contains information about employment, educational qualifications, income, integration experiences, and household socioeconomic conditions. Particularly relevant for researching ethnic and migration-related stratification, labor market inequalities, social integration, and differences in economic opportunities between migrant and nonmigrant populations in Germany during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: IAB-BAMF-SOEP Survey of Refugees, 2016–2025
justification: A longitudinal survey focusing on refugees who arrived in Germany, particularly during the migration movements of the mid-2010s. It collects information about educational backgrounds, occupational experience, labor market participation, household income, language proficiency, and social integration. The dataset is especially useful for studying socioeconomic stratification among refugee populations and comparing their educational and employment trajectories with those of other groups in Germany throughout the late 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUScompact), 2023
justification: A more accessible, anonymized version of the 2023 German General Social Survey. It contains information about social structure, demographic characteristics, occupational categories, education, income, values, and attitudes. Particularly relevant for studying contemporary social groupings, class identification, and perceptions of inequality in Germany. Its standardized structure also makes it suitable for comparisons with earlier ALLBUS survey waves.

returned_title: German Microcensus, 2018 Scientific Use File
justification: A specific research dataset from the German Microcensus that is particularly useful for examining social stratification in the late 2010s. It includes detailed socioeconomic and demographic information suitable for investigating occupational class, employment, education, household characteristics, and regional social inequalities. Researchers have used German Microcensus data to study spatial differences in social class and residential patterns. This release provides a useful pre-pandemic reference point for comparisons with data from the 2020s.
