returned_title: GESIS Panel.pop: Longitudinal Population Survey, 2013–Present
justification: A continuing German population panel containing repeated measurements of attitudes, behavior, and social characteristics. Its multiple recruitment cohorts allow researchers to explore how socioeconomic position relates to political attitudes, group identification, social trust, and perceptions of social divisions. Particularly useful for investigating emerging social groupings and changes in social attitudes across the 2010s and 2020s. The panel also includes research addressing social experiences during the COVID-19 period.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), International and EU Editions
justification: The official data access page for the German Socio-Economic Panel, offering different editions of the longitudinal dataset. These files provide detailed information on income, employment, educational background, household composition, migration, and socioeconomic circumstances. They are particularly suitable for analyzing income classes, poverty, social mobility, and inequalities across population groups during the 2010s and 2020s. The available editions differ in geographic detail and access conditions.

returned_title: German Health Update (GEDA) 2010–2020 – Robert Koch Institute
justification: One of the most relevant sources for studying general health and well-being in Germany during the 2010s and 2020s. The Robert Koch Institute (RKI) provides nationally representative health survey datasets for 2010, 2012, 2014/2015, and 2019/2020. Variables cover self-rated health, chronic illnesses, health behaviors, healthcare utilization, and physical and mental health. Scientific Use Files provide individual-level research data, subject to access requirements.

returned_title: German Health Update (GEDA 2019/2020-EHIS) – Open Data
justification: An openly available dataset containing aggregated health indicators from Germany's 2019–2020 European Health Interview Survey. It includes information on physical and mental health, health behaviors, and population health differences by age, gender, education, and federal state. Data are available in CSV format, making this particularly useful for quantitative analysis of health inequalities and population well-being immediately before and during the early COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: German Health Update (GEDA) – Scientific Use Files 2010, 2012, 2014/2015, and 2019/2020
justification: The official RKI landing page provides detailed descriptions of individual GEDA survey waves and their Scientific Use Files. These datasets support comparisons of health status, health-related behaviors, and healthcare access across different periods. The 2019/2020 wave contains 22,708 respondents and 310 variables. Particularly suitable for examining changes in health and well-being between the early 2010s and 2020.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2025
justification: A major longitudinal household survey covering Germany from 1984 through 2025, including the entire 2010s and the first half of the 2020s. The dataset includes self-reported health, health satisfaction, general life satisfaction, employment, household income, education, and socioeconomic conditions. Its longitudinal structure allows researchers to investigate how individuals' health and subjective well-being change over time and how these changes relate to economic and social circumstances. Access is subject to research data agreements.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 1980–2025
justification: A nationally representative repeated cross-sectional survey examining social conditions, attitudes, and behaviors in Germany. The ALLBUS series includes surveys throughout the 2010s and 2020s, with a cumulative dataset available through 2023 and a separate 2025 wave. Relevant variables include subjective well-being, social relationships, socioeconomic circumstances, and health-related measures in selected waves. Useful for studying the social determinants of well-being and changes in quality of life across population groups. Registration is required to download survey data.

returned_title: Eurostat – Self-Perceived Health by Sex, Age and Labour Status
justification: An official European statistical dataset measuring individuals' assessments of their general health. It provides data covering 2008–2025, including Germany throughout the 2010s and 2020s. Observations can be disaggregated by sex, age, and employment status. Particularly useful for analyzing trends in perceived health, demographic health inequalities, and differences between Germany and other European countries. Data are accessible through Eurostat's online database.

returned_title: Eurostat – Overall Life Satisfaction by Sex, Age and Educational Attainment
justification: A European statistical dataset covering overall life satisfaction from 2013 to 2025, including Germany. Life satisfaction is measured on a scale from 0 to 10, with breakdowns by age, sex, and educational attainment. This dataset directly addresses subjective well-being and quality of life. It is particularly valuable for examining changes in happiness and life satisfaction during the 2010s and 2020s, including differences between demographic and socioeconomic groups.

returned_title: Eurostat – European Union Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC)
justification: A comprehensive European household survey covering income, living conditions, health, and social inclusion, with German observations throughout the 2010s and 2020s. Relevant measures include self-perceived health, chronic health conditions, limitations in daily activities, material deprivation, and socioeconomic circumstances. The dataset is especially useful for analyzing connections between financial well-being, social inequality, and health. Access to scientific-use microdata requires an application.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults (DEGS1)
justification: A nationally representative German adult health survey conducted around the beginning of the 2010s. The DEGS1 dataset includes 7,987 respondents and 1,033 variables, covering physical health, chronic diseases, health-related behaviors, and other health indicators. It provides a useful baseline for understanding population health in Germany during the early 2010s. Particularly suitable for detailed analyses of adult health and comparisons with later RKI surveys.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Children and Adolescents (KiGGS), Waves 1 and 2
justification: A major health monitoring study focusing on children and adolescents aged 0–17 in Germany. Wave 1 covers 2009–2012, while Wave 2 provides observations from the mid-2010s. The surveys include indicators of physical health, mental health, health behaviors, and socioeconomic conditions. These datasets are especially useful for examining health inequalities and well-being among younger populations during the 2010s, complementing the adult-focused GEDA surveys.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulative Dataset 1980–2023
justification: A harmonized cumulative dataset combining multiple waves of Germany's General Social Survey through 2023. It enables longer-term comparisons of subjective well-being, social integration, living conditions, and selected health-related indicators. The cumulative format is particularly useful for comparing the 2010s with the early 2020s without having to combine separate survey files manually. Researchers should check variable availability and question consistency across survey years.

returned_title: Eurostat – Self-Perceived Health by Sex, Age and Citizenship
justification: An official Eurostat dataset providing self-reported health indicators differentiated by age, sex, and citizenship group. It includes observations for Germany during the 2020s and can support investigations of health disparities between population groups. Particularly useful for research on migration-related health inequalities, population diversity, and differences in perceived general health.

returned_title: Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core) – EU Edition, 1984–2025
justification: The EU Edition of Germany's longitudinal Socio-Economic Panel provides household and individual survey data, including health satisfaction, life satisfaction, income, employment, and living conditions. It covers the 2010s and 2020s through 2025. The dataset is particularly suitable for investigating relationships between socioeconomic changes, subjective well-being, and health over time. Its repeated observations enable individual-level longitudinal analysis. Access requires an appropriate data-use agreement.

returned_title: German Family Panel (pairfam) – Panel Analysis of Intimate Relationships and Family Dynamics, 2008–2022
justification: One of the most comprehensive longitudinal datasets on family life and intimate relationships in Germany. Covers 14 survey waves from 2008 to 2022, including the entire 2010s and early 2020s. Contains information on marriage, cohabitation, relationship satisfaction, separation, divorce, fertility intentions, parenting, and intergenerational relationships. Particularly useful for studying how family structures and marriage patterns changed over time. Individual-level research data are available through GESIS under a data-use agreement.

returned_title: FReDA – The German Family Demography Panel, 2021–2025
justification: A major longitudinal survey specifically designed to study contemporary family life and demographic change in Germany. The referenced release includes survey waves collected between 2021 and 2025. Covers partnerships, marriage, fertility, family planning, parenting, relationship quality, household arrangements, and gender roles. Particularly valuable for analyzing family formation, changing marriage expectations, and family dynamics during the 2020s. It also supports continuity with the earlier German Family Panel (pairfam).

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core) – Longitudinal Household and Family Data
justification: A nationally representative longitudinal household survey covering Germany since 1984. This dataset version includes observations through 2021, making it suitable for analyzing family and marriage trends throughout the 2010s and into the 2020s. Contains information on marital status, household composition, partnerships, children, employment, household income, life satisfaction, and socioeconomic inequalities. Especially useful for investigating relationships between marriage, family structures, economic conditions, and well-being. Research access conditions apply.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Annual Marriage Statistics in Germany, 1950–2025
justification: Official annual marriage statistics published by the German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis). Provides the number of marriages and marriage rates per 1,000 inhabitants, covering the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for examining long-term marriage trends, changes in marriage frequency, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on marriage patterns. Data can be used for time-series analysis and comparisons between periods.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Marriages by German Federal State, 1990–2025
justification: Official regional marriage statistics covering all German federal states. Provides annual marriage counts from 1990 through 2025, including the requested decades. Particularly valuable for studying geographical differences in marriage patterns, comparing eastern and western Germany, and examining regional changes in marriage frequency. Suitable for regional demographic research and longitudinal statistical analysis.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Annual Divorce Statistics in Germany, 1950–2025
justification: Official German divorce statistics providing annual counts of legally finalized divorces. Includes continuous observations across the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for investigating marital stability, divorce trends, and changes in family dissolution patterns. Can be combined with marriage statistics to compare trends in marriage formation and dissolution. Particularly relevant for examining whether divorce frequency changed during the COVID-19 period.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Divorces by Duration of Marriage, 1982–2025
justification: Official divorce statistics classified by the duration of marriage before divorce. Covers both the 2010s and 2020s and allows researchers to investigate marital stability at different relationship durations. Particularly useful for analyzing whether shorter or longer marriages became more likely to end in divorce and for identifying changes in the distribution of marriage duration at dissolution.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Divorces and Children Affected by Divorce
justification: Official statistical collection containing divorce datasets, including table 12631-0003 on divorces classified by the number of joint minor children. Relevant for examining the relationship between marital dissolution and family life during the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for studying divorces involving children and understanding how changes in divorce patterns may affect families with dependent children.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Family Structures and Living Arrangements in Germany (Microcensus)
justification: Official German Microcensus statistics on family structures and household living arrangements. Includes married couples with and without children, unmarried cohabiting couples, single parents, and other family arrangements. Particularly relevant for examining changes in the prevalence of marriage, cohabitation, single parenthood, and childless partnerships. Provides a foundation for studying structural changes in German family life across the 2010s and 2020s. Researchers should account for methodological changes introduced with the 2020 Microcensus redesign.

returned_title: Destatis – Families and Family Members with Minor Children by Living Arrangement
justification: Official statistical tables describing German families with minor children, distinguishing married couples, cohabiting couples, and single-parent households. Includes comparisons between eastern and western Germany. Useful for investigating family composition, the importance of marriage in households with children, and regional differences in family arrangements. Particularly relevant for understanding contemporary family structures in the 2020s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) 2012 – Family and Changing Gender Roles IV
justification: International comparative survey dataset containing German respondents and focusing on family attitudes and gender roles. Covers attitudes toward marriage, parenting, women's employment, household responsibilities, partnerships, and the division of labor within families. Particularly useful for examining German social attitudes toward family life during the early 2010s. Enables comparisons between Germany and other countries, as well as comparisons with earlier ISSP family survey waves.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme – Family and Changing Gender Roles, 1988–2022
justification: A collection of internationally comparable survey datasets examining changing attitudes toward family life, marriage, gender roles, parenting, and domestic responsibilities. Includes survey rounds from 2012 and 2022, making it particularly useful for comparing family-related attitudes between the 2010s and 2020s. Researchers can select German respondents to investigate changing expectations surrounding marriage, household labor, parenthood, and gender equality. The collection also supports longer-term comparisons using earlier survey rounds.

returned_title: Destatis – Marriages, Divorces and Registered Life Partnerships in Germany
justification: Official German Federal Statistical Office data portal covering marriage, divorce, and registered life partnerships. Provides access to statistical tables and historical series relevant to the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for investigating marriage trends, marital dissolution, and changes in legally recognized partnerships, including developments following the introduction of same-sex marriage in Germany in 2017. Serves as a central access point for multiple official marriage and divorce datasets.

returned_title: Destatis – Households and Families in Germany
justification: Official statistical data portal focusing on household composition, family structures, couples, children, and living arrangements in Germany. Provides access to Microcensus-based statistical tables and information on family types, including married couples, unmarried partnerships, and single-parent households. Useful for analyzing changes in German family structures during the 2010s and 2020s and for identifying relevant datasets on household size, children, and family composition.

returned_title: Destatis – Passenger Transport in Germany (2019–2024)
justification: Official German Federal Statistical Office dataset covering passenger transport by buses, trams, railways, aviation, and private motor vehicles. Provides annual passenger numbers and enables comparisons of transport demand before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS – Public Passenger Transport by Bus and Rail (2004–2024)
justification: Official annual dataset covering public passenger transport in Germany, including passengers carried, passenger-kilometres, vehicle-kilometres, transport capacity, and transport companies. Covers the entire 2010s and early 2020s, making it valuable for studying long-term public transport trends.

returned_title: Eurostat – Railway Passenger Transport (2004–2025)
justification: Eurostat dataset containing annual railway passenger transport statistics, including passenger numbers and passenger-kilometres. Includes Germany throughout the 2010s and 2020s and supports comparisons with other European countries. Particularly useful for studying railway demand, mobility changes, and the pandemic's effects.

returned_title: Eurostat – Air Passenger Transport by Type of Schedule, Transport Coverage and Country
justification: Official European dataset containing German aviation passenger statistics from 1993 onward, including observations during the 2010s and 2020s. Provides monthly, quarterly, and annual information on air passengers, scheduled flights, and domestic and international aviation. Useful for analyzing aviation growth, international travel, and the pandemic-related decline in air travel.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS – Tourist Arrivals, Overnight Stays and Average Length of Stay (1992–2025)
justification: Official annual tourism dataset covering arrivals, overnight stays, and average accommodation duration in Germany. Includes continuous observations throughout 2010–2025. Particularly suitable for studying tourism growth, domestic travel, COVID-19 disruptions, and the recovery of Germany's accommodation sector.

returned_title: Destatis – Tourist Arrivals and Overnight Stays by Guest Residence and Accommodation Type
justification: Official German tourism statistics made discoverable through the European Data Portal. Provides tourist arrivals, overnight stays, and average stay duration, differentiated by guest residence and accommodation category. Useful for examining domestic versus international tourism and changes in accommodation preferences.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS – Tourist Arrivals and Overnight Stays by Federal State and Month
justification: Official regional tourism dataset containing monthly arrivals and overnight stays across Germany's federal states, with distinctions by guest residence. Useful for analyzing regional tourism differences, seasonal travel patterns, and the recovery of tourism destinations during the 2020s.

returned_title: Mobility in Germany (Mobilität in Deutschland – MiD 2017 and 2023)
justification: Major nationwide household travel survey commissioned by the German Federal Ministry of Transport. The 2017 and 2023 survey waves provide information on daily trips, transport modes, travel distances, travel purposes, household characteristics, and mobility behavior. Earlier surveys from 2002 and 2008 support longer-term comparisons. Particularly valuable for investigating changes in German travel habits between the 2010s and 2020s. Detailed survey documentation and information about data access are available through the project website.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS – Road Traffic Accidents in Germany (2008–2025)
justification: Official annual dataset of police-recorded road traffic accidents throughout Germany. Provides accident counts differentiated by severity and location, including urban roads, rural roads, and motorways. Covers the 2010s and 2020s, allowing analysis of road safety trends, traffic disruptions, and changes associated with reduced mobility during the pandemic.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS – Road Traffic Accidents by German Federal State (2008–2025)
justification: Regional road safety dataset covering all 16 German federal states. Contains annual accident counts classified by accident category and road location. Suitable for analyzing geographical differences in road traffic safety and comparing accident trends across regions during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS – Road Traffic Accidents with Injuries and Fatalities by Month (2011–2026)
justification: Detailed monthly road accident statistics covering accidents involving personal injury and the number of casualties, differentiated by accident type, location, and injury severity. Useful for investigating seasonal patterns, changes in road safety, and the effects of major disruptions on travel and transport.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS – Motor Vehicle and Trailer Registration Statistics
justification: Official German statistics covering registered motor vehicles, passenger cars, vehicle types, fuel categories, and new registrations. Includes national and regional breakdowns. Relevant for studying car ownership, motorization, electric vehicle adoption, and structural changes in road transport during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Passenger Cars per Thousand Inhabitants
justification: European transport dataset measuring passenger car ownership relative to population. Includes Germany and other European countries, enabling comparisons of motorization levels across the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for studying long-term changes in private car dependence and transport accessibility.

returned_title: Eurostat – Passenger Cars by Type of Motor Energy
justification: Eurostat dataset classifying passenger cars according to fuel or propulsion technology. Includes Germany and supports analysis of the transition from petrol and diesel vehicles toward electric and alternative-fuel vehicles. Particularly relevant for examining sustainable transport developments during the 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Road Traffic by Vehicle Type
justification: European road transport dataset containing road traffic measurements differentiated by vehicle category. Includes Germany and provides a basis for examining changes in road transport activity, traffic intensity, and the relative importance of different vehicle types.

returned_title: Destatis – Monthly Tourism Overnight Stays in Germany
justification: Official German short-term tourism statistics tracking overnight stays in accommodation establishments. Provides monthly indicators useful for analyzing tourism seasonality, short-term travel demand, and recovery patterns following the COVID-19 pandemic. Complements annual tourism datasets with higher-frequency observations.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS – Inland Waterway Freight Transport Statistics
justification: Official German dataset covering freight transport on inland waterways, including goods transported, freight volumes, transport performance, ports, and shipping routes. Contains annual and monthly statistical tables relevant to transport activity during the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for analyzing freight mobility, logistics, and the role of river transport in Germany.

returned_title: Destatis – Passenger Transport Statistics, Statistical Report 2024
justification: Official statistical publication and data resource covering passenger transport in Germany for 2024. Provides detailed transport statistics that complement longer-running GENESIS time series. Useful for examining public transport activity and passenger mobility in the post-pandemic period.

returned_title: German Environment Agency (UBA) – Environmental Data in Germany
justification: Official German federal environmental data portal providing datasets, indicators, and historical trends on Germany's natural environment. Covers air quality, water resources, soil conditions, biodiversity, land use, climate change, and environmental pollution. Contains data relevant to both the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for analyzing nationwide environmental changes and comparing environmental indicators across years.

returned_title: German Weather Service (DWD) – Climate Data Center
justification: Official repository of historical and recent climate observations across Germany. Includes temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, sunshine duration, and other meteorological variables. Provides station-level observations and gridded climate datasets covering the 2010s and 2020s. Suitable for studying climate variability, extreme weather, droughts, and long-term environmental changes.

returned_title: German Environment Agency – Air Quality in Germany: Open Data
justification: Official air pollution monitoring data from the German Environment Agency. Provides measurements of major atmospheric pollutants, including particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, and ozone. Historical observations support analyses of air quality changes during the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for investigating atmospheric environmental conditions, pollution trends, and regional differences across Germany.

returned_title: CORINE Land Cover – Germany
justification: Official German environmental dataset describing land cover and land use. Includes reference datasets for 2012, 2015, and 2018. Identifies forests, agricultural land, grasslands, wetlands, water bodies, and artificial surfaces. Useful for measuring changes in natural habitats, urban expansion, agricultural landscapes, and ecosystem fragmentation during the 2010s.

returned_title: Copernicus Land Monitoring Service – CORINE Land Cover
justification: European land cover datasets that include Germany and provide standardized geographical classifications. Historical editions include 2012 and 2018, alongside land cover change products. Data can be filtered geographically to Germany. Particularly useful for assessing deforestation, habitat conversion, agricultural land use, wetland distribution, and changing natural landscapes.

returned_title: German Aerospace Center (DLR) – CORINE Land Cover Germany
justification: Geospatial land cover dataset provided by the German Aerospace Center. Offers standardized classifications of natural and human-modified landscapes in Germany. Supports investigation of land cover dynamics, forest distribution, agricultural expansion, and changes in natural ecosystems. Relevant for spatial environmental analyses of the 2010s.

returned_title: Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) – Biodiversity Data for Germany
justification: International biodiversity database containing species occurrence records from Germany. Includes observations of plants, animals, fungi, and other organisms contributed by scientific institutions and biodiversity monitoring initiatives. Records can be filtered by observation date to isolate the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for studying species distributions, biodiversity patterns, and changes in ecological communities.

returned_title: GBIF Germany – National Biodiversity Data Network
justification: German national biodiversity information network facilitating access to species records and biodiversity datasets from research institutions, museums, and environmental monitoring organizations. Provides access to information relevant to Germany's terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. Useful for identifying datasets on wildlife, vegetation, species occurrence, and biodiversity monitoring during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: High-Resolution Climate Data for the German National Forest Inventory (1961–2020)
justification: Research dataset providing daily climate time series across Germany at a spatial resolution of approximately 250 meters. Derived from German Weather Service observations and covering 1961–2020, including the entire 2010s and 2020. Particularly valuable for investigating relationships between temperature, precipitation, forest conditions, ecosystem vulnerability, and environmental change.

returned_title: DWD Climate Data Center – Historical and Recent Monthly Climate Observations
justification: Monthly meteorological observations collected from monitoring stations throughout Germany. Includes climate variables relevant to natural environmental conditions, such as temperature and precipitation. Historical and recent datasets allow comparisons across the 2010s and 2020s. Appropriate for analyzing seasonal climate patterns, temperature trends, rainfall variability, and regional environmental differences.

returned_title: DWD Climate Data Center – Hourly Air Temperature Observations
justification: High-frequency air temperature observations from weather stations across Germany. Historical and recent measurements enable analysis of temperature fluctuations during the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for identifying heatwaves, temperature extremes, climate anomalies, and local environmental conditions.

returned_title: DLR Earth Observation Center – Environmental and Land Monitoring Datasets
justification: German Aerospace Center geospatial data catalogue containing satellite-derived environmental information. Includes land cover, vegetation, forests, water bodies, snow cover, and other Earth observation products. Several datasets provide temporal coverage relevant to the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for monitoring changes in Germany's natural landscapes, ecosystems, and environmental conditions.

returned_title: DWD Climate Data Center – German Climate Reference Data (1995–2012)
justification: Gridded meteorological reference dataset covering Germany for 1995–2012. Provides climate information suitable for characterizing local environmental conditions and establishing historical reference conditions. Includes the beginning of the 2010s and can serve as a baseline when comparing subsequent environmental and climatic changes.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online: Employment by Economic Sector in Germany (1991–2025)
justification: Official dataset from Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), providing annual employment figures by economic sector. Includes employees, self-employed persons, and contributing family workers. Covers the entire 2010s and 2020–2025, making it particularly useful for analyzing long-term employment trends, structural changes in the German economy, and sectoral employment patterns.

returned_title: Eurostat: Employment and Labour Force by Sex and Age – Annual Data
justification: Official European Union Labour Force Survey dataset containing annual employment indicators for Germany, disaggregated by sex and age group. Suitable for studying employment rates, demographic differences, female labour force participation, and changes in employment during the 2010s and 2020s. Also enables comparisons between Germany and other European countries.

returned_title: Eurostat: Employment and Labour Force by Sex and Age – Quarterly Data
justification: Quarterly Labour Force Survey dataset providing employment indicators for Germany by sex and age. Its higher temporal frequency makes it useful for studying short-term employment fluctuations, the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, and labour market recovery during the 2020s. Particularly relevant for time-series analysis.

returned_title: Eurostat: Unemployment by Sex and Age – Annual Data
justification: Official Eurostat dataset providing annual unemployment rates and unemployment counts by sex and age, including Germany. Covers the 2010s and 2020s and supports analysis of youth unemployment, gender disparities, and changes in unemployment following economic shocks. Uses internationally comparable labour market definitions.

returned_title: Eurostat: Unemployment by Sex and Age – Quarterly Data
justification: Quarterly unemployment dataset covering Germany and other European countries, with breakdowns by demographic characteristics. Useful for examining seasonal and cyclical unemployment, the economic effects of COVID-19, and labour market developments throughout the 2010s and 2020s. DOI: 10.2908/une_rt_q.

returned_title: Eurostat: Unemployment Rate – Annual Data
justification: Harmonized annual unemployment rate dataset based on International Labour Organization definitions. Includes German observations from the 2010s through 2025. Particularly suitable for investigating long-term unemployment trends, economic cycles, and Germany's labour market performance relative to other EU member states.

returned_title: German Federal Employment Agency: Employment and Labour Market Statistics
justification: Official statistics portal of the German Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit). Provides extensive administrative labour market datasets, including unemployment, registered employment, job vacancies, short-time work, and regional labour market indicators. Historical time series cover the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly valuable for detailed analysis at national, federal-state, district, and local levels.

returned_title: Deutsche Bundesbank: Employment and Labour Market Time Series
justification: Official German central bank statistical collection containing employment and unemployment time series, including employed persons, employees subject to social security contributions, and registered unemployment. Offers downloadable time-series data suitable for analyzing Germany's labour market developments during the 2010s and 2020s and their relationship with macroeconomic conditions.

returned_title: IAB: Sample of Integrated Labour Market Biographies (SIAB 7523)
justification: Longitudinal administrative microdataset from Germany's Institute for Employment Research (IAB). Contains a 2% random sample of individuals represented in the Integrated Employment Biographies, covering 1975–2023. Records employment histories, unemployment, benefit receipt, job seeking, and labour market programme participation. Highly relevant for examining employment mobility, job stability, unemployment transitions, and individual labour market trajectories during the 2010s and early 2020s. Access is restricted to approved research arrangements.

returned_title: IAB: Sample of Integrated Labour Market Biographies – Regional File (1975–2023)
justification: Research dataset based on German administrative employment records, providing longitudinal information on employment and unemployment histories. Its regional variables make it useful for investigating geographical differences in labour market conditions, regional employment mobility, and employment inequalities across Germany during the 2010s and early 2020s. Available as a factually anonymized scientific-use dataset subject to access conditions.

returned_title: IAB: Establishment Panel (IAB-BP), 1993–2024
justification: Longitudinal establishment-level survey dataset maintained by the Institute for Employment Research. Covers German businesses and workplaces, including information about employment structures, recruitment, training, working conditions, and establishment characteristics. The 1993–2024 coverage enables analysis of employer behaviour, workforce adjustments, skill shortages, and employment trends throughout the 2010s and early 2020s. Research access restrictions apply.

returned_title: IAB: Establishment History Panel (BHP)
justification: Administrative longitudinal dataset containing information on establishments employing workers covered by German social security records. Particularly useful for analyzing employment growth, establishment size, workforce composition, regional employment structures, and changes in labour demand during the 2010s and 2020s. The dataset supports detailed employer-level research but requires authorized access.

returned_title: IAB: German Job Vacancy Survey (IAB-SE)
justification: Establishment survey dataset providing information on job vacancies, recruitment activity, hiring difficulties, and labour demand in Germany. Relevant for investigating labour shortages, skills mismatches, employer recruitment behaviour, and changes in hiring conditions during the 2010s and 2020s. Especially valuable for studying Germany's labour market tightness and workforce shortages.

returned_title: IAB: Panel Study Labour Market and Social Security (PASS)
justification: Longitudinal household and individual survey dataset examining employment, unemployment, social security, and economic circumstances in Germany. Includes information relevant to labour market participation, job transitions, benefit receipt, and social inequality. Particularly suitable for analyzing relationships between employment status, household conditions, and social protection during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: IAB: Linked Employer-Employee Data (LIAB)
justification: Linked administrative and survey dataset connecting individual employment histories with information about German establishments. Supports analysis of wages, employment mobility, worker characteristics, employer behaviour, and workplace inequality. Particularly useful for investigating how firm-level characteristics influenced employment outcomes and labour market developments during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core v41): Data 1984–2024
justification: Major representative longitudinal household survey conducted by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin). Contains individual-level information on employment status, occupational histories, earnings, working hours, education, and household income. The 1984–2024 coverage makes it especially valuable for investigating labour market inequality, gender wage gaps, employment transitions, and the socioeconomic consequences of labour market changes throughout the 2010s and early 2020s.

returned_title: Destatis: Labour Force by Sex, Age, Employment Type, and Other Characteristics
justification: Official German labour force dataset available through the European Data Portal and sourced from Destatis. Provides employment and labour force information disaggregated by demographic and employment-related characteristics. Useful for analyzing labour force participation, differences between population groups, and employment structures in Germany during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: IAB: Panel of Establishments in the COVID-19 Crisis (IAB BeCovid)
justification: Specialized employer-level panel dataset examining how German establishments responded to the COVID-19 crisis. Relevant for studying changes in employment, recruitment, workplace organization, and business adjustment strategies during the early 2020s. Particularly useful for research comparing pandemic-related labour market disruptions with pre-pandemic conditions.

returned_title: IAB: IAB-ZEW Labour Market 4.0 Establishment Survey
justification: Establishment-level research dataset focusing on technological change, digitalization, and their implications for employment in Germany. Suitable for investigating how automation and digital technologies affect workforce composition, skill requirements, and labour demand. Provides valuable evidence for understanding structural labour market transformations associated with the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: IAB: IAB-ZEW Start-up Panel
justification: Research panel dataset covering German start-ups and young enterprises, including information relevant to employment creation and business development. Useful for examining entrepreneurship, job creation, hiring behaviour, and the contribution of newly established businesses to employment during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2012 (Germany)
justification: A nationally representative survey conducted by the German Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (BIBB) and the Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (BAuA). Contains detailed information on physical and psychological working conditions, occupational demands, workplace stress, job satisfaction, qualifications, and health complaints. Particularly useful for establishing a baseline of working conditions in Germany during the early 2010s.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 (Germany)
justification: A comprehensive survey of German employees covering working conditions, occupational health, physical and psychological demands, workplace organization, job satisfaction, and employment characteristics. Provides detailed individual-level data for analyzing working conditions in the late 2010s and comparing them with earlier survey waves.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2024 (Germany)
justification: A recent wave of Germany's major employment and working conditions survey. Covers workplace demands, occupational stress, physical and psychological working conditions, job satisfaction, and employment characteristics. Particularly valuable for examining changes in working conditions during the 2020s and comparing them with the 2012 and 2018 surveys.

returned_title: Harmonised BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2006, 2012 and 2018
justification: A harmonized dataset combining three waves of Germany's employment surveys. Standardized variables facilitate comparisons of occupational demands, working environments, employment characteristics, and job satisfaction across survey years. Especially valuable for studying changes in German working conditions throughout the 2010s.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2015 (Germany)
justification: A German national survey focusing on working hours and their relationship with employee health and well-being. Includes information on weekly working hours, overtime, shift work, flexible working arrangements, psychological and physical job demands, and work-life balance. Provides an important baseline for studying working-time conditions before the COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2017 (Germany)
justification: The 2017 wave of the BAuA Working Time Survey examines working schedules, overtime, flexibility, workplace demands, and employee well-being. Its panel design supports longitudinal research on changing working conditions and working-time arrangements in Germany.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2019 (Germany)
justification: Provides detailed information about German employees' working hours, shift arrangements, flexibility, workplace demands, job satisfaction, and health. Particularly useful as a pre-pandemic reference point for analyzing changes in working conditions during the 2020s.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2021 (Germany)
justification: Captures working-time arrangements, flexibility, occupational demands, and employee well-being during the COVID-19 period. Useful for investigating changes in working conditions, work-life balance, working schedules, and workplace organization in Germany during the early 2020s.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2023 (Germany)
justification: Provides recent individual-level evidence on working hours, flexible schedules, psychological and physical workplace demands, employment conditions, and employee well-being. Particularly valuable for assessing post-pandemic working conditions and comparing developments across the 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, and 2023 waves.

returned_title: European Working Conditions Survey (EWCS) 2010
justification: A European survey conducted by Eurofound that includes German respondents. Covers working hours, occupational health and safety, physical and psychosocial workplace risks, work organization, training, and job satisfaction. Useful for comparing Germany's working conditions with those of other European countries at the beginning of the 2010s.

returned_title: European Working Conditions Survey (EWCS) 2015
justification: Provides harmonized survey data on working conditions across European countries, including Germany. Includes measures of work intensity, physical risks, psychosocial demands, working-time quality, employment conditions, and occupational well-being. Particularly valuable for international comparisons and investigating working conditions during the mid-2010s.

returned_title: European Working Conditions Telephone Survey (EWCTS) 2021
justification: A cross-national survey examining working conditions during the COVID-19 pandemic, including Germany. Covers job quality, working arrangements, work-life balance, health, and employee well-being. Useful for studying pandemic-related workplace changes and comparing Germany with other European countries. Researchers should account for methodological differences from earlier face-to-face EWCS waves.

returned_title: European Working Conditions Survey (EWCS) 2024
justification: The 2024 wave of Eurofound's European Working Conditions Survey provides recent evidence about job quality and working environments across Europe, including Germany. Particularly relevant for examining working conditions in the mid-2020s, investigating post-pandemic developments, and comparing German employees' experiences with those in other European countries.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2022, Teaching Edition
justification: A longitudinal household panel survey covering Germany over several decades. Includes detailed information on employment status, earnings, working hours, job satisfaction, occupational characteristics, health, and socioeconomic circumstances. Its annual observations make it particularly valuable for investigating trends in employment quality and working conditions throughout the 2010s and early 2020s. The teaching edition is designed for educational research and has more limited information than the full research dataset.

returned_title: IAB Establishment Panel (IAB-Betriebspanel), 1993–2018
justification: An annual representative survey of German establishments conducted by the Institute for Employment Research (IAB). Contains employer-level information on workforce composition, employment arrangements, personnel policies, training, working-time practices, and organizational characteristics. Particularly useful for studying structural changes in German workplaces and employer practices throughout the 2010s.

returned_title: IAB Establishment Panel (IAB-Betriebspanel), 1993–2023
justification: A longitudinal employer survey covering establishments throughout Germany, with observations extending into the 2020s. Provides information on employment structures, workforce management, training, organizational practices, and workplace policies. Valuable for examining changes in employment conditions from an employer perspective. The linked IAB research data documentation describes the dataset and its research access arrangements.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP): Work Orientations IV, 2015
justification: An internationally harmonized survey containing a German sample. Examines job satisfaction, employment preferences, working conditions, workplace relationships, job security, work-related attitudes, and work-life balance. Particularly useful for analyzing subjective assessments of working conditions in Germany and comparing German workers with employees in other countries. Registration is required to download the data.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP): Work Orientations I–IV, 1989–2015, Cumulated Dataset
justification: A harmonized longitudinal collection of repeated cross-sectional surveys examining employment attitudes and experiences, including observations from Germany. Covers job satisfaction, work preferences, employment security, and attitudes toward working life. Useful for placing working conditions in the 2010s within a longer historical context and identifying changes in workers' perceptions over time.

returned_title: German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis): Quality of Employment Indicators
justification: Official German statistical indicators concerning employment quality, including excessive working hours and related employment characteristics. Provides aggregated data suitable for examining trends in German working conditions during the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful for descriptive analyses and supplementing individual-level survey datasets with official national statistics.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Surveys 2006–2024: Interactive Working Conditions Data
justification: An interactive data resource providing selected results from the German employment surveys conducted in 2006, 2012, 2018, and 2024. Includes indicators concerning working conditions, occupational demands, workplace resources, job satisfaction, and health complaints. Supports customized tables and visualizations with download options. Especially useful for quickly comparing working conditions across the 2010s and 2020s without processing the full survey microdata.

returned_title: International Labour Organization: Key Indicators of the Labour Market (KILM)
justification: An international database providing standardized labor market indicators for Germany and other countries. Relevant variables include average working hours, part-time employment, labor costs, productivity, and employment characteristics. Provides historical time series covering the 2010s and 2020s, making it useful for examining broader changes in employment conditions and comparing Germany with other economies.

returned_title: Destatis – Tourism in Germany: Monthly Arrivals and Overnight Stays (2010s–2020s)
justification: Official dataset from Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), covering monthly tourist arrivals and overnight stays in accommodation establishments. Includes domestic and international visitors. Particularly useful for analyzing tourism trends across the 2010s and 2020s, including the impact of COVID-19 and subsequent recovery.

returned_title: Destatis – Tourist Arrivals and Overnight Stays by German Federal State
justification: Official German tourism statistics providing monthly arrivals and overnight stays across Germany's federal states (Bundesländer). Includes distinctions between domestic and foreign visitors. Suitable for analyzing regional tourism patterns, geographical differences, seasonal fluctuations, and changes in tourism demand during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Nights Spent at Tourist Accommodation Establishments (Monthly Data)
justification: Harmonized European tourism dataset providing monthly overnight stays in hotels, holiday accommodation, and camping establishments. Germany can be selected individually. Includes data covering the 2010s and 2020s, allowing comparisons of tourism activity before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Particularly useful for time-series analysis and international comparisons.

returned_title: Eurostat – Nights Spent at Tourist Accommodation Establishments (Annual Data)
justification: Annual tourism dataset covering overnight stays by domestic and international tourists across European countries, including Germany. Enables analysis of long-term tourism development, accommodation preferences, and differences between domestic and inbound tourism during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Participation in Tourism for Personal Purposes (2012–2025)
justification: Official Eurostat dataset measuring participation in tourism for personal purposes among European residents, including Germany. Covers 2012–2025 and provides information on tourist participation, trip duration, and destinations. Particularly relevant for studying changes in Germans' holiday participation and travel behavior across the two decades.

returned_title: Eurostat – Tourism Trips by Main Destination
justification: Dataset covering tourism trips by destination country or world region. German residents' travel can be analyzed by selecting Germany as the reporting country. Useful for investigating domestic and international holiday preferences, changing travel destinations, and tourism behavior during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Number of Tourism Trips by EU Residents
justification: Annual dataset measuring the number of tourism trips undertaken by residents of European countries, including Germany. Supports analysis of domestic versus outbound tourism, personal versus business travel, and changes in trip frequency. Particularly valuable for investigating the decline in travel during 2020 and subsequent recovery.

returned_title: Destatis – German Time Use Survey 2012/2013 and 2022 (Zeitverwendungserhebung)
justification: One of the most relevant official German datasets for studying leisure activities. The surveys conducted in 2012/2013 and 2022 measure how individuals allocate time to work, household responsibilities, sports, hobbies, entertainment, cultural activities, and social interactions. Particularly useful for comparing leisure behavior across the 2010s and 2020s. Published aggregate statistics are available, while access to detailed microdata is provided through the official research data center.

returned_title: Destatis – Time Spent on Activities by Age Group, Germany 2022
justification: Official statistical table from the 2022 German Time Use Survey, providing average time spent on different activities by age group. Includes sports, hobbies, games, and other leisure-related activities. Useful for investigating generational differences in leisure participation and how recreational behavior varies across demographic groups.

returned_title: Destatis – German Time Use Survey 2022: Activity Classification
justification: Official classification of activities recorded in Germany's 2022 Time Use Survey. Provides definitions and categories for leisure, physical activities, hobbies, and other daily activities. This resource is especially valuable when interpreting the survey data or constructing comparable leisure and sport indicators. It is a supporting classification rather than a standalone statistical dataset.

returned_title: Destatis – Cultural and Leisure Time Use Comparison, 2012/2013 and 2022
justification: Official German statistical comparison of time spent on cultural activities using the 2012/2013 and 2022 Time Use Surveys. Includes activities such as reading and other forms of cultural engagement. Particularly suitable for comparing cultural leisure participation between the 2010s and 2020s and examining differences by gender.

returned_title: GESIS – German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2010s and 2020s
justification: Long-running representative survey of Germany's population, conducted approximately every two years. Includes survey waves from the 2010s and 2020s, with information on social behavior, attitudes, demographics, and other aspects of everyday life. Selected waves and variables can support research on leisure-related behavior and social participation. Individual-level datasets are available through GESIS, generally requiring free registration.

returned_title: Foundation for Future Issues – German Leisure Monitor (Freizeit-Monitor)
justification: German longitudinal survey series examining leisure behavior, recreational preferences, and the popularity of different leisure activities. Includes findings from the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly relevant for investigating how Germans spend their free time, including entertainment, social activities, digital leisure, and recreational pursuits. Published survey findings and statistical summaries are available, although access to underlying respondent-level data is not established.

returned_title: Eurostat – Tourism Accommodation Statistics and Data Collection
justification: Official Eurostat portal providing access to tourism datasets covering accommodation occupancy, tourism trips, overnight stays, and travel expenditure. Includes Germany and supports comparisons across the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly useful as a central entry point for discovering additional tourism indicators and understanding their statistical definitions.

returned_title: Destatis – Tourism Statistics in Germany
justification: Official German statistical portal covering tourism and hospitality. Provides access to tourism statistics, accommodation data, arrivals, overnight stays, and related economic indicators. Offers historical information relevant to the 2010s and more recent statistics from the 2020s. Particularly useful for locating additional official datasets and publications concerning Germany's tourism industry.

returned_title: Eurostat – Regional Tourism Statistics in Germany and Europe
justification: Regional tourism dataset measuring overnight stays in tourist accommodation establishments across European NUTS 2 regions, including German regions. Suitable for examining regional tourism intensity, comparing German tourist destinations, and investigating geographical changes in tourism demand over time. Particularly relevant for regional analysis during the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Robert Koch Institute – Physical Activity and Sport Participation in German Population Studies
justification: Research overview identifying German population datasets collected between 1993 and 2024 that include physical activity, sport participation, and active leisure indicators. Covers studies relevant to both the 2010s and 2020s, including the German Ageing Survey and health monitoring surveys. Particularly useful for identifying suitable primary datasets for studying recreational exercise, sport participation, and demographic differences. This is a dataset discovery resource rather than a directly downloadable dataset.

returned_title: German Panel on Household Finances (PHF) – Deutsche Bundesbank (2010–2023)
justification: One of the most comprehensive datasets for studying income, property ownership, wealth, investment, and savings in Germany. The survey covers five waves: 2010/2011, 2014, 2017, 2021, and 2023. Variables include household income, real estate ownership and values, mortgages, financial assets, savings accounts, stocks, bonds, pension assets, debts, and household demographics. Particularly useful for analyzing changes in wealth distribution, property ownership, and investment behavior between the 2010s and 2020s. Anonymized microdata are available to researchers upon request.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core) – DIW Berlin (1984–2023)
justification: A major longitudinal household survey covering Germany, with annual observations throughout the 2010s and into the 2020s. Includes household and individual income, employment, housing conditions, housing costs, homeownership, and sources of income. Selected waves also contain detailed wealth information. Particularly valuable for examining income inequality, economic mobility, housing affordability, and relationships between income and accumulated wealth. Access to detailed microdata requires registration and compliance with research data agreements.

returned_title: Household Finance and Consumption Survey (HFCS) – European Central Bank (2010–2023)
justification: A harmonized European household finance survey that includes Germany. Survey waves cover 2010, 2014, 2017, 2021, and 2023. Contains detailed information on household income, real estate, mortgages, financial investments, bank deposits, bonds, shares, pension savings, liabilities, and net wealth. Especially useful for comparing German household wealth and investment patterns with those of other European countries. Research microdata are available through an application process.

returned_title: Sample Survey of Income and Expenditure (EVS) – German Federal Statistical Office (2013, 2018, 2023)
justification: An official German household survey conducted every five years. The 2013, 2018, and 2023 waves are especially relevant for comparing household finances across the two decades. Covers household income, consumption expenditure, real estate assets, financial wealth, savings, and household debt. Useful for studying how German households allocate income between consumption, housing, and wealth accumulation. The source provides documentation for the different survey waves.

returned_title: German Household Real Estate and Financial Assets – Destatis EVS (2018–2023)
justification: Official statistics on German household wealth, with particular emphasis on property ownership and real estate values. Includes information about the market value of residential property and changes between 2018 and 2023. Suitable for investigating property wealth accumulation, changes in the housing market, and the role of real estate in household balance sheets. Especially relevant for studying property-related developments during the 2020s.

returned_title: EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC) – Eurostat (2004–2023)
justification: A harmonized European microdataset containing German household income and living conditions. The 2024 release covers cross-sectional observations from 2004 to 2023, including the 2010s and early 2020s. Variables cover disposable income, income sources, poverty, housing tenure, housing costs, and socioeconomic characteristics. Particularly useful for analyzing income inequality, differences between homeowners and renters, and housing affordability. Detailed research microdata require authorization.

returned_title: EU-SILC Public Microdata – Eurostat
justification: Provides publicly accessible sample microdata for European income and living conditions statistics, including Germany for selected years. Contains household-level and individual-level files covering income, demographics, and housing conditions. Useful for exploring data structures, testing statistical analyses, and examining relationships between household characteristics and economic outcomes. These public-use files have limitations and should not be treated as substitutes for the full research microdata when producing representative estimates.

returned_title: Income in Real Terms (2010 SILC = 100) – Eurostat
justification: An official Eurostat annual dataset measuring changes in real income relative to a 2010 reference. Includes Germany and other European countries, with coverage extending through the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for analyzing real household income developments while accounting for inflation. Particularly suitable for comparing changes in German purchasing power across time and against other European economies.

returned_title: Income and Receipts of Private Households (EVS) – Destatis GENESIS-Online
justification: An official statistical table presenting household income and receipts in Germany, differentiated by household size and survey year. Based on the German Sample Survey of Income and Expenditure. Useful for studying differences in income levels across household types during the 2010s and 2020s. The GENESIS database provides structured statistical tables suitable for quantitative analysis and downloading.

returned_title: Household Saving Rate – Eurostat (2014–2025)
justification: An annual macroeconomic dataset measuring gross household savings as a percentage of household disposable income, with an adjustment for pension entitlements. Includes Germany and other European economies. Particularly useful for analyzing changes in German saving behavior before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Provides a consistent indicator for comparing savings trends across the late 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Key Indicators for Sector Accounts – Annual Data (nasa_10_ki) – Eurostat
justification: A comprehensive annual national accounts dataset covering household income, savings, investment, and financial indicators. Includes German household saving rates, household investment rates, disposable income indicators, and debt-to-income ratios. Particularly useful for examining macroeconomic relationships between household income, saving, and investment throughout the 2010s and 2020s. Appropriate for time-series analysis and international comparisons.

returned_title: Key Indicators for Sector Accounts – Quarterly Data (nasq_10_ki) – Eurostat
justification: Quarterly European national accounts indicators covering household savings, investment, and financial positions, including Germany. Particularly valuable for investigating short-term changes in household saving and investment during major economic events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, inflationary pressures, and changing interest rates. The quarterly frequency supports more detailed analysis than annual datasets.

returned_title: Private Consumption Expenditure of Households – Destatis (1998–2023)
justification: Official German household expenditure statistics covering multiple years, including 2013, 2018, and 2023. Provides detailed household spending information, including housing, energy, maintenance, food, and other consumption categories. Useful for understanding how household expenditure patterns affect the amount of income available for savings and investment. Particularly relevant when studying the relationship between housing costs and household financial capacity.

returned_title: Private Consumption Expenditure for Basic Needs by Territory – Destatis EVS (2008–2023)
justification: Provides German household expenditure data for 2008, 2013, 2018, and 2023, distinguishing between Germany overall, former West German territories, and eastern Germany including Berlin. Includes spending on housing, energy, food, and other basic needs. Useful for comparing regional differences in living costs and assessing their implications for household disposable income and potential savings.

returned_title: German Household Income, Assets and Debts – EVS 2023
justification: Official information about the redesigned 2023 German Sample Survey of Income and Expenditure. The survey collects data on income, household consumption, real estate assets, financial wealth, and debts. Particularly relevant for detailed analysis of German household financial positions in the 2020s. The 2023 survey can be compared with earlier EVS waves, although methodological changes must be considered when interpreting trends.

returned_title: Panel on Household Finances (PHF) – Bundesbank Research Data and Scientific Use Files
justification: The official research data access page for the German Panel on Household Finances. Provides information about obtaining anonymized household microdata covering 2010/2011, 2014, 2017, 2021, and 2023. The dataset is especially valuable for examining income, residential and other real estate, financial investments, savings behavior, mortgages, and household net wealth. Researchers can request individual survey waves or combined data, making it particularly suitable for longitudinal research on German wealth accumulation and financial inequality.

returned_title: Destatis – Sample Survey of Income and Expenditure (EVS): Private Consumption Expenditure in Germany, 2013, 2018 and 2023
justification: One of the most relevant official datasets for studying household consumption in Germany during the 2010s and 2020s. Published by the German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), it provides household consumption expenditure for 2013, 2018 and 2023, including spending on food, housing, clothing, transport, recreation and other categories. Particularly useful for comparing changes in household budgets, spending priorities and consumption patterns across the two decades.

returned_title: Eurostat – Household Final Consumption Expenditure by Purpose (COICOP 1999)
justification: Official European statistical dataset providing annual household consumption expenditure by purpose, with data covering 1975–2025 and including Germany. Expenditure is classified into categories such as food, clothing, housing, transport, communications, health and recreation. Particularly useful for analyzing long-term changes in German consumption patterns between 2010 and 2025 and comparing Germany with other European countries.

returned_title: Destatis – Continuous Household Budget Surveys (Laufende Wirtschaftsrechnungen, LWR)
justification: Official German household budget statistics providing detailed information on private consumption expenditure across multiple years in the 2010s and 2020s. The surveys complement the larger EVS studies and provide more frequent observations of household expenditure. Useful for investigating changing spending patterns, consumption by household characteristics and the effects of economic developments on household budgets.

returned_title: Eurostat – Internet Purchases by Individuals, 2002–2019
justification: European statistical dataset measuring online purchasing behavior among individuals, including residents of Germany. Covers 2002–2019, making it particularly valuable for examining the development of e-commerce throughout the 2010s. Includes indicators related to the frequency of online purchases and characteristics of online shopping behavior. Useful for analyzing the digital transformation of German consumer behavior before the COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: Eurostat – Internet Purchases by Individuals, 2020 Onwards
justification: Official Eurostat dataset covering online purchasing behavior from 2020 onward, including observations for Germany through 2025. Provides indicators on internet shopping participation and purchasing behavior, with demographic breakdowns. Particularly useful for examining changes in German e-commerce during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Can be used alongside the predecessor dataset for 2002–2019, although methodological differences should be checked before combining the series.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Monthly Retail Trade Turnover Index in Germany (45212-0004)
justification: Official German retail trade dataset providing monthly turnover indices by retail sector, with coverage extending from 1994 into the 2020s. Includes nominal and real turnover indicators for different retail activities. Particularly useful for examining changes in German purchasing activity, retail consumption trends, seasonal shopping patterns, the effects of COVID-19 and subsequent inflation-related changes in consumer spending.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Annual Retail Trade Turnover Index in Germany (45212-0003)
justification: Annual German retail trade dataset covering the entire 2010s and much of the 2020s, with figures available through 2025. Provides nominal and inflation-adjusted retail turnover indices across different economic sectors. Particularly appropriate for comparing retail consumption before and after the pandemic and investigating structural changes in German shopping behavior.

returned_title: Destatis – Equipment of German Households with Information and Communication Technology
justification: Official dataset measuring ownership and availability of information and communication technology in German households. Includes EVS observations for 2013, 2018 and 2023, alongside observations from continuous household budget surveys. Covers products and technologies such as computers, laptops, tablets and internet access. Useful for examining technology adoption, durable-goods consumption and the digitalization of German households.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core v29) – Household Consumption Module
justification: Research dataset from the German Socio-Economic Panel, administered by DIW Berlin. This release includes the HCONSUM dataset derived from the household consumption module introduced in 2010. It enables detailed analysis of household consumption in relation to income, employment, household composition and socioeconomic characteristics. Particularly useful for individual- and household-level research into the determinants of consumer behavior in Germany during the early 2010s. Access to microdata is subject to the provider's conditions.

returned_title: GESIS Panel – Longitudinal Survey Data on the German Population
justification: Longitudinal survey infrastructure providing repeated observations of the German-speaking adult population, with data collected from 2014 onward. The GESIS Panel covers a broad range of social attitudes and individual behaviors, with relevant variables available for selected consumption-related research questions. Particularly useful for studying consumer attitudes, preferences and behavioral changes in relation to demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Researchers should examine the questionnaires to identify the specific consumption-related variables available.

returned_title: Eurostat – Quarterly Final Consumption Expenditure of Households and NPISH, Current Prices
justification: Quarterly European national accounts dataset measuring household and nonprofit institution final consumption expenditure at current prices. Includes Germany and provides a useful macroeconomic measure of consumption activity throughout the 2010s and 2020s. Particularly suitable for examining quarterly fluctuations in household consumption, the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent changes in nominal consumption expenditure.

returned_title: Eurostat – Quarterly Final Consumption Expenditure of Households and NPISH, Volumes
justification: Quarterly consumption dataset providing volume-based indicators of household final consumption expenditure, including Germany. Particularly useful for analyzing changes in real consumption while reducing the influence of price inflation. Supports research on economic cycles, pandemic-related consumption shocks and the recovery of household spending during the 2020s. Complements nominal expenditure data by distinguishing real consumption developments from price effects.

returned_title: Destatis – Private Consumption Expenditure in Germany: Long-Term National Accounts Series
justification: Official German national accounts dataset providing long-term annual private consumption expenditure statistics, including observations throughout the 2010s and 2020s. Contains expenditure indicators by consumption purpose and associated changes over time. Useful for studying long-term trends in household consumption, identifying shifts in spending across categories and placing recent consumer behavior within a broader historical context.

returned_title: Destatis – Internet Use and Online Shopping in Germany, 2021–2025
justification: Official German statistical table containing data on private internet use and online shopping behavior from 2021 to 2025. Particularly relevant for studying the growing importance of digital consumption and e-commerce among German consumers. Provides a national perspective on changing internet shopping participation during the 2020s and complements Eurostat's harmonized e-commerce datasets.

returned_title: Destatis – Household Consumption Expenditure by Household Size
justification: Official German household expenditure statistics differentiated by household size. Includes information from the Sample Survey of Income and Expenditure and the Continuous Household Budget Surveys. Particularly useful for comparing consumption patterns between single-person households, couples and larger households during the 2010s and 2020s. Supports research on household composition, economies of scale and differences in spending priorities across demographic groups.

returned_title: Germany Energy Balance Data (1990–2025) – AG Energiebilanzen
justification: Official German energy balance statistics covering the 2010s and 2020s. Includes primary energy consumption, energy supply, electricity generation, fossil fuels, renewable energy, and energy consumption by sector. Particularly useful for analyzing Germany's energy transition, changes in fossil fuel dependence, and long-term energy consumption trends.

returned_title: Germany Electricity Generation and Energy Market Data – Fraunhofer ISE Energy-Charts
justification: Provides downloadable historical electricity generation and market data for Germany, including solar, wind, coal, natural gas, nuclear, and other energy sources. Covers relevant years in the 2010s and 2020s, with detailed time-series information. Suitable for examining renewable energy expansion, electricity prices, and changes in Germany's electricity generation mix.

returned_title: Eurostat Complete Energy Balances (1990–2024)
justification: Comprehensive annual energy balance dataset covering Germany from 1990 through 2024. Includes energy production, imports, exports, transformation, and final consumption across individual energy products. Allows detailed analysis of Germany's energy supply, fossil fuel dependence, renewable energy adoption, and sectoral energy consumption during both decades.

returned_title: Eurostat Simplified Energy Balances (1990–2024)
justification: Provides harmonized annual statistics on energy production, consumption, imports, exports, and energy transformation. Germany-specific observations are available for 2010–2024. Useful for comparing energy consumption across economic sectors and examining structural changes in Germany's energy system.

returned_title: Germany Renewable Energy Statistics – Umweltbundesamt (German Environment Agency)
justification: Official German government statistics on renewable energy development, including electricity, heating, and transport. Provides historical time series covering the 2010s and 2020s, with downloadable data from the Working Group on Renewable Energy Statistics (AGEE-Stat). Useful for studying solar, wind, hydropower, biomass, and Germany's renewable energy transition.

returned_title: Renewable Energy Sources in Germany – Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
justification: Official government resource providing access to statistics and historical time series on renewable energy development in Germany. Includes information on installed renewable generation capacity, renewable electricity production, and renewable energy use in heating and transport. Relevant for analyzing renewable energy growth throughout the 2010s and 2020s.

returned_title: Eurostat Economy-Wide Material Flow Accounts (1990–2025)
justification: Highly relevant natural resources dataset covering domestic extraction, imports, exports, and consumption of materials. Includes biomass, metal ores, non-metallic minerals, and fossil energy materials. Germany-specific observations cover the 2010s and 2020s. Useful for studying natural resource extraction, resource efficiency, material consumption, and Germany's transition toward a circular economy.

returned_title: Eurostat Domestic Material Consumption per Capita
justification: Provides annual indicators of domestic material consumption per person, including Germany. Derived from Eurostat's material flow accounts, the dataset helps measure natural resource use relative to population.
